bearerAuth.description: A secret API key from your dashboard (your plan sets how many): `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…`. Publishable widget keys (`pk_live_…`) work only for the endpoints widgets read, each from the one site it names.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Your plan's request quota for the current period (on paid plans a month counted from the day and time the plan started, on Free the UTC day).

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests still available in the current period.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the period ends and the quota refills.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

Fixture.description: A single match. Every endpoint and every WebSocket snapshot returns it in this same shape.

sport.description: Slug of the sport, matching the values listed by /v2/sports.

startTime.description: Kick-off time. Holds the scheduled start until the source logs the actual kick-off, which then takes its place (the live feed delivers it a few minutes after play begins). Identical across all endpoints and WebSocket deltas. Matches from before 1970 have one too (they read null until 2026-11-23).

endTime.description: The moment the match finished according to the source's records. Stays null while the match is unfinished, and for a match whose finishing time the source never logged. A match spread over several days, such as a cricket Test, shows up in /v2/fixtures?date= for each day between startTime and endTime. Fixtures saved before 2026-11-26 read null until they are fetched again. Available since 2026-11-26.

league.description: Competition the fixture belongs to. It is null if the source places the fixture in a competition that has no matching league (observed in minor regional football, e.g. South Africa’s National Second Division on 2026-10-23); in that case season and round are null as well.

season.description: The season the source places the fixture in. When a league runs a competition of its own within its season, those games sit in that competition's season: NBA Cup group games belong to "NBA Cup 2026" with its group tables, and the conference and division tables stay with the regular season. /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons lists both.

round.description: Round of the fixture, for competitions organised in rounds.

homeRecord.description: In the US leagues (NFL, NBA, NHL), the home team’s season record as it stands for this game: the "9-4" (in the NHL the W-L-OTL "15-5-2") a broadcast prints beside the team’s name. Null in every other competition. Available since 2026-11-20.

awayRecord.description: The away team’s season record, on the same terms. Available since 2026-11-20.

playerOfTheMatch.description: Cricket’s official player of the match once it has been announced; null before that and in other sports (football’s fan vote is served by /best-players). Available since 2026-11-20.

levels.description: Competition levels our data source assigns to the fixture’s competition ("topCompetitions", "pro", "youth", …), so top-level, professional or youth fixtures can be filtered without keeping a list of leagues. An empty list when it assigns none. Available since 2026-11-20.

tier.description: Tennis only: "lower" marks an event of the Challenger or ITF tier and null a tour-level one; always null in other sports. Available since 2026-11-20.

group.description: Name of the group when the match is part of a group stage ("Group A", as in the round robin of the ATP Finals), otherwise null. The group’s matches are listed by /v2/leagues/{id}/groups/{groupId}/fixtures. Available since 2026-11-20.

stage.description: Where inside the season the source places the match, if that is somewhere below the league: a qualifier ("UK Championship Qualifiers 2026"), a stage like the playoffs ("NWSL, Playoffs") or a fight card. For a one-off tournament that has no league (league null) it carries the tournament’s name (since 2026-11-24). Null when the match sits straight under its league. It is text to show, not a key to match on; fixtures stored before it existed read null until they are fetched again. Available since 2026-11-23.

home.description: The home team. Null until that slot is settled, e.g. while the source still shows a placeholder like "WQF1" (winner of quarter-final 1).

away.description: The away team. Null until that slot is settled (for instance a "WQF1" placeholder from the source).

homeMembers.description: Doubles in tennis, padel, badminton and table tennis: the two players who make up the home pair, ordered as the source gives them. Each of them is a competitor in their own right (a TeamRef of kind individual, at /v2/teams/{id}, with the id their singles matches and rankings use). Null for a single competitor or a team, for a side still to be decided, and when the source’s answer leaves the players out (some lists, and fixtures stored before 2026-11-23 that have not been read since). Available since 2026-11-23.

awayMembers.description: The two players of the away pair, on the same terms as homeMembers. Available since 2026-11-23.

winner.description: Stays null until status.type is finished, and also when a fight ends as a no contest (`fightResult.method` noContest). When penalties decide the match, this is always the shoot-out winner regardless of the source (which, on a second leg, reports the team that won the 90 minutes). If the source omits the winner, or declares a draw in a sport where draws are impossible (finishes in regular time or overtime; cricket excluded), we derive it from the score.

venue.description: Where the match is played, if known (frequently null in lower divisions). Populated on /fixtures/{id}, and in date lists when the source provides it. Round, team, player and live lists never include a venue, so a null there means "omitted" rather than "unknown" — fetch /fixtures/{id} to get it.

clock.description: The match clock. Null if the source keeps no clock for this fixture, and after the match ends.

firstToServe.description: Deprecated (2026-10-23); mirrors `serving`. Because the source refreshes it each game / leg, it reflects who is serving (throwing) at the moment, not who served first. Use `serving` instead.

serving.description: Tennis, darts and other sports with a serve: which side is currently serving (throwing), refreshed by the source every game / leg. Null if the source gives no indication.

servedFirst.description: Darts: which side threw the opening dart of the match (`serving` is whoever is throwing now). Fixed for the whole match once play begins; null before that, when the source does not say, and in every other sport (only darts data carries it). Since 2026-11-11.

homeSeed.description: For seeded events such as tennis draws or playoff brackets (basketball, …): the seed of the home side ("1", "12") or the way it entered ("Q" qualifier, "WC" wild card, "LL" lucky loser, "PR" protected ranking, …), exactly as shown in the draw. Null for an unseeded side.

awaySeed.description: Seed or entry status of the away side; see homeSeed.

homeRanking.description: Ranking of the home side as the source attaches it to the fixture. On UFC bouts: the fighter’s position in the division’s rankings when the bout took place, with 0 for the champion. Tennis players (since 2026-11-23): their ATP or WTA singles position, the one shown in the `atp` / `wta` lists of /v2/rankings rather than the live lists, taken from the source’s most recent reply about the match; doubles pairs and unranked players get null. Other sports (since 2026-11-23): the side’s own standing where the source keeps one, such as the world ranking of a rugby team. Since 2026-11-23 lists carry it as well, as the side’s present-day ranking. For a match that is over, /v2/fixtures/{id} gives the rank the side held on match day; since 2026-11-28 lists show that same match-day rank too, as soon as the fixture has been opened once with /v2/fixtures/{id}, and until then they keep today’s rank (MMA lists: null instead, since today’s rank is homeCurrentRanking). Null when no ranking is attached, as for most fixtures. Available since 2026-11-18.

awayRanking.description: Ranking of the away side; see homeRanking. Available since 2026-11-18.

homeCurrentRanking.description: MMA fixture lists only: where the home fighter sits in his division today, as of the list's latest refresh (0 is the champion). After the bout this can drift away from `homeRanking`, the rank he held on fight night. Null on /v2/fixtures/{id} (which keeps the fight-night rank), in other sports and for a fighter with no rank. Available since 2026-11-25.

awayCurrentRanking.description: Today's division rank of the away fighter; see homeCurrentRanking. Available since 2026-11-25.

note.description: Cricket: the match note supplied by the source, which becomes the result line at the end ("Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by 37 runs"). Intended for display only.

battingSide.description: Cricket: which side is currently at the crease. Null outside a live innings and in every other sport.

fightResult.description: MMA / boxing: how, in which round and at what time the fight ended. Null before status.type reaches finished, and when the source supplies no method.

fightDiscipline.description: Combat sports: the bout’s discipline, when the source labels it (the `mma` sport includes boxing, kickboxing and Muay Thai cards as well). Only some cards are labelled (ONE, Queensbury, certain OKTAGON fights; never UFC or PFL), so a null value does not imply MMA.

referee.description: Match official, if the source names one (football and a few other sports; in cricket, the match referee). Present on /fixtures/{id}; always null in lists, where it is omitted.

homeManager.description: Manager or head coach of the home side as named in the source’s fixture, which means whoever leads the team NOW. Up to and during the match that coincides with the person in charge of it; once a finished match is read after a change of manager, the successor appears instead. The managers of the match itself are on /v2/fixtures/{id}/managers. Present on /fixtures/{id}; null in lists.

awayManager.description: Current manager or head coach of the away side; behaves like homeManager.

surface.description: Tennis: the surface the match is played on. Present on /fixtures/{id} and in live lists; null in other sports.

discipline.description: Tennis: singles or doubles, or team for a tie between two nations made of several rubbers (since 2026-11-24; a client that only knows singles and doubles should treat an unknown value as neither). Present on every fixture endpoint, in lists and in WebSocket snapshots; null in other sports and when the source specifies neither. Since 2026-11-11.

toss.description: Cricket: the toss result, after it has taken place. Present on /fixtures/{id}; null in other sports.

umpires.description: Cricket: the on-field umpires, named as the source writes them (frequently with a country code, e.g. "Asif Yaqoob (PAK)"). Null when none are listed and in other sports.

tvUmpire.description: Cricket: the TV (third) umpire, formatted as for umpires.

previousLegFixtureId.description: Two-legged ties and playoff series: the DataSportsAPI id of the preceding leg / game, when the source links the two. Look that id up on /fixtures/{id} to get the first-leg score.

parentFixtureId.description: Tennis team competitions (Davis Cup, Billie Jean King Cup): on a singles or doubles rubber, the fixture id of the nations’ tie it is part of, and the tie itself has discipline team. The source makes the link late, often just before the rubber starts, so expect null until then. Null on every other match. Available since 2026-11-24.

matchesInTie.description: For knockout ties and playoff series: the number of matches the tie is decided over, if the source states it — 1 for a one-off match, 2 for a two-legged football cup tie, 7 for a best-of-seven basketball series. Null on a league fixture, whenever the source is silent about it, and on any fixture stored before 2026-11-18 until it is fetched again. Related: previousLegFixtureId. Available since 2026-11-18.

aggregateWinner.description: Once the return leg of a two-legged tie is over: the side that went through. Taken from the source’s verdict when available; otherwise from `aggregated` (the higher total advances) or, if the aggregate is level, from the shoot-out. Null in every other case, including a level aggregate the source leaves unresolved (an away-goals rule). Compare `winner`, which refers to this match alone: when a second leg goes to penalties both fields name the shoot-out winner, but otherwise they can disagree (a side may win the second leg yet be eliminated). Filled on /fixtures/{id}; in lists and live snapshots it can be null.

fightCard.description: MMA / boxing: the bout’s section of the card, its running order and its weight class, if the source lists them.

attendance.description: Crowd figure, if the source reports one (observed for NBA and MLB games, frequently only after the game has started). Present on /fixtures/{id}; omitted (null) in lists. A finished match is read again for up to 8 hours after the final whistle (since 2026-11-23), so a crowd figure the source adds late, as for NFL games, still arrives.

matchFormat.description: Darts and esports: the format of the match (best of N sets / legs / games), if the source states it. Null in other sports.

inningState.description: Baseball: the live game situation — inning, half, balls, strikes, outs and runners on base. Null unless the game is in progress or interrupted, and null in every other sport. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas.

timeouts.description: Basketball and, since 2026-11-23, American football: timeouts each side has left, and the one being taken (`active`). Null outside an in-progress or interrupted game, and whenever the source does not track them. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas.

downAndDistance.description: American football: the current down, distance and field position. Null unless the game is in progress or interrupted, and null in every other sport. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-09.

varCheck.description: Football: an ongoing VAR review. Null when no review is under way, outside play and in other sports. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-09.

bonus.description: Basketball: whether each side is in the bonus. Null outside an in-progress or interrupted game, and whenever the source does not report it. The source’s live feed never carries it, so it appears in REST responses and lists only. Available since 2026-11-09.

finalResultOnly.description: True if the source provides only the final result for this fixture, with no live score, clock or events during play (available since 2026-11-09).

stale.description: true for a match the source shows as running although it has gone quiet: no change in 45 minutes, and kick-off longer ago than any match in that sport could take. Such a match is already missing from /v2/livescores and the WebSocket; the date, league, team and fixture endpoints still report the source's status, with this flag set, so treat it as finished rather than live. false otherwise. Available since 2026-11-23.

awarded.description: `true` when the result was awarded rather than played — a forfeit, or a ruling by a disciplinary body or federation. The score is then the awarded one (usually 3–0, or whatever the score was when an abandoned match was allowed to stand), and `status` shows finished just as for a played match. `false` for a result decided on the field and for a fixture still to finish. Fixtures stored before 2026-11-18 carry null until they are fetched again (finished fixtures keep their stored copy). Available since 2026-11-18.

durations.description: Sports played in sets or rounds: the length of every finished period (available since 2026-11-04). Null for sports the source does not time by period (football, basketball, …) and until the first period is over. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas.

awayFirst.description: Whether the source names this competition's visitors first, the "Away @ Home" style of the North American leagues (NFL, NBA, NCAA, NHL, AHL and some baseball leagues): true there, false where the home side comes first. Handy for ordering the two sides the way local fans read them; the tracker widget follows it. Fixtures saved before 2026-11-26 read null until they are fetched again. Available since 2026-11-26.

addedTime.description: Sports with a running clock, such as football: the stoppage minutes the officials announced for each period, keyed as in ScoreSide.periods (period1 and period2 for the halves, extra1 / extra2 for the two halves of extra time). A period's figure stays here once it is over, whereas clock.injuryTimeMinutes only covers the period being played and turns null at a break, so the first half's added time can still be read at half-time and after the match. Null when nothing was announced, and on fixtures saved before 2026-11-26 until they are fetched again. WebSocket deltas carry the periods that change. Unit: minutes. Available since 2026-11-26.

lineupsAvailable.description: Becomes true when the source publishes lineups for the fixture, whether predicted or official (check `confirmed` on /v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups to tell them apart), and false if they are withdrawn. We set it the moment the source’s live feed announces lineups, or when a lineup we fetch contains players. Null means we have no information yet (no announcement observed, nothing fetched). WebSocket deltas carry it live — on fixture:{id} from before kick-off, and on the list channels once play starts. After the final whistle the flag keeps the value it had during play, in REST and in every list (until 2026-11-26 it turned null there). Available since 2026-11-04.

lineupsConfirmed.description: Becomes true when the official lineups are released (matching `confirmed` on /v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups); otherwise behaves like lineupsAvailable, with null meaning we have no information. Delivered live via WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-04.

tiesInRound.description: Knockout stages: how many ties the round holds, which is how the source codes it: 1 for a final, 2 for semi-finals, 4 for quarter-finals, 8 for the last 16, 16 for the last 32. Null in league play and wherever the source leaves the round uncoded. Carried by every fixture endpoint and by WebSocket snapshots and deltas; null on fixtures saved before 2026-11-27 until they are read again. Available since 2026-11-27.

xgAvailable.description: true when the source holds expected-goals figures for this match, which then appear in /v2/fixtures/{id}/statistics and on the shot map; null when it gives no answer either way. Carried by every fixture endpoint and by WebSocket snapshots and deltas; null on fixtures saved before 2026-11-27 until they are read again. Available since 2026-11-27.

playerStatisticsAvailable.description: true when the source keeps a statistics line per player for this match, read through /v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups; null when it gives no answer either way. Carried by every fixture endpoint and by WebSocket snapshots and deltas; null on fixtures saved before 2026-11-27 until they are read again. Available since 2026-11-27.

playerHeatmapAvailable.description: true when the source keeps a heatmap per player for this match; null when it gives no answer either way. Carried by every fixture endpoint and by WebSocket snapshots and deltas; null on fixtures saved before 2026-11-27 until they are read again. Available since 2026-11-27.

currentBatterId.description: During a live cricket innings, the batter the source marks as current, given as our player id. That mark moves back and forth between whoever faces the coming delivery and whoever faced the previous one, so treat it as a batter at the crease, not a guaranteed striker. Names and figures are on /v2/fixtures/{id}/scorecard (ScorecardInnings.currentBatter). Read from the fixture detail; the live feed does not push it. Null otherwise, in other sports, and on rows stored before 2026-11-27 until their next refresh. Since 2026-11-27.

currentBowlerId.description: During a live cricket innings, the bowler the source marks as current, given as our player id: whoever has the over under way or has just completed one. Null in the same cases as currentBatterId. Since 2026-11-27.

FixtureSummary.description: A short form of a fixture with just what a schedule row needs: the two sides, when it starts, how far it has got and the score. /v2/fixtures/summary returns it; /v2/fixtures/{id} has everything else. Available since 2026-11-24.

id.description: Our fixture id, the one /v2/fixtures/{id} takes.

league.description: The competition, as its id and name; null when the fixture has no league.

home.description: The home side: id, name and the short code a scoreboard uses; null while the side is still to be decided.

away.description: The away side, in the same form as home.

status.description: Where the match stands, the same value as Fixture.status.type.

homeScore.description: The home side’s current score (Fixture.homeScore.current); null until it has one.

awayScore.description: The away side’s current score, on the same terms.

type.description: High-level state, computed from `phase` (mapping in the StatusPhase table).

code.description: The source’s raw status code (the data dictionary lists every value); `phase`, `period` and `finish` give you its meaning ready-made.

description.description: Human-readable English label taken from our status table (status codes in the data dictionary) and adapted to the sport, for example "Halftime", "2nd half", "After penalties", "After extra time" (football), "After extra innings" (baseball), "After overtime" (basketball, ice hockey, …), "1st innings" (cricket) or "Coverage canceled". For a code we do not recognise, the source’s own wording is passed through. Use it for display, never for branching logic.

period.description: Period currently being played, or the one just completed during a break. Null before the start and after the end. When the source announces a break (status code 31) without naming the period behind it, since 2026-11-25 we fill it by sport: period1 where there are two halves, period2 in four-quarter sports (basketball, water polo, American football, aussie rules), and in ice hockey and floorball the latest period anyone has scored in (null if nobody has yet; a WebSocket delta leaves the period out in that case, so keep yours). A period the source does name always wins.

finish.description: The way the result was reached. Only set when `type` is finished; null otherwise.

current.description: The headline score you would see on a scoreboard: goals, points, sets won (tennis / volleyball) or runs (cricket, baseball), counting extra time / overtime. Shoot-out goals are excluded and reported in `penalties` instead — except in ice hockey and, since 2026-11-23, floorball, where the shoot-out winner is given one extra goal (3-3 after overtime becomes 3-4). Once a match is under way neither side is null: a side still waiting for its first score reads 0 (since 2026-11-24; earlier, lists and frames could show null). Before the start, for fights (MMA keeps no score) and for fixtures whose coverage was canceled, it is null.

periods.description: The score split by period and keyed by PeriodKey — goals per half, quarter or period; games per set in tennis; points per set in volleyball and table tennis; runs per inning in baseball. Extra periods are included too: football and futsal use `extra1` / `extra2`; American football, basketball, handball, ice hockey, water polo and others use `overtime`; baseball extra innings run from `period10` upwards (`overtime` only if the source reports extra-innings runs as one total). When the source’s breakdown is complete the values sum to `current`; it is occasionally incomplete (some baseball leagues omit innings, a few futsal matches lack a half), and ice hockey or floorball decided by a shoot-out is intentionally one goal short (see `current`). Rugby: the source provides the half scores only at full time; during play period1 is set at half-time (the score at that moment), and once the second half is under way period2 is current minus period1; if we first pick up a fixture after the break, both stay empty until the final whistle (the score at half-time remains readable on the period entry in /v2/fixtures/{id}/events). Esports uses one key per game (map), with a title-dependent meaning: Counter-Strike and Dota 2 usually store 1 for each map a side won and 0 for the rest (maps not played count as 0, through period5 in a best of 3), but on events the source follows round by round (best-of-one matches, and the PGL Major since 2026-11-25) the value is how many rounds the side took on that map (13 / 6); in League of Legends it is the side’s kill count in game N, so the values do not sum to `current`, which counts games won. Each game’s winner and score are on /fixtures/{id}/games. Empty when the source gives no breakdown.

tieBreaks.description: Tennis: points won in each set’s tie-break, using the same keys as `periods` (e.g. { "period2": 7 }).

normalTime.description: Score when regulation time ended, if the source provides it.

penalties.description: Goals converted in a penalty shoot-out. In ice hockey and floorball the shoot-out winner gets 1 here and the loser 0, in line with the single goal added to `current`.

aggregated.description: Combined score across both legs of a two-legged tie.

series.description: Playoff series: number of games this side has won in the series to date (basketball, baseball, ice hockey, water polo).

point.description: Tennis: score within the current game — "0" | "15" | "30" | "40" | "A", or a plain number ("0"–"N") during a tie-break. Darts: the points the side still has to score in the current leg ("501" when a leg starts). Null when play is neither in progress nor interrupted.

redCards.description: Football: number of red cards this side has received, counting second yellows. Once the match is under way it starts at 0 rather than null, on REST and, since 2026-11-26, in WebSocket deltas as well.

innings.description: Cricket: each innings of this side, keyed inning1…N. Empty in other sports.

hits.description: Baseball: hit total, i.e. the H in the R/H/E line.

errors.description: Baseball: error total, i.e. the E in the R/H/E line.

CricketInnings.description: A single cricket innings played by one side.

wickets.description: Number of wickets that have fallen.

overs.description: Overs delivered, in cricket notation (49.5 means 49 overs plus 5 balls).

targetRunRate.description: Run rate the chasing side needs to reach its target.

Clock.description: Timing data for a match. Running clocks (football, rugby, …): compute elapsed = periodOffsetSeconds + (now − periodStartedAt) and minute = floor(elapsed / 60) + 1; once periodEndSeconds is passed, display periodEndSeconds / 60 followed by "+" and the extra minutes. This applies only while status.phase is inprogress. Stop clocks (basketball, handball, ice hockey, …): playedSeconds is the value at playedAt and advances only while `running` is true. Tennis, table tennis, badminton and esports (set / map sports) carry only `periodStartedAt` (start of the current set or map), and only if the source sends it — the clock as a whole is frequently null. A field is null whenever the source does not provide it for that sport; the entire clock is null when no clock exists and after the match ends. Lists other than /fixtures/{id} may include fewer clock fields (static values such as periodLengthSeconds can be null there).

periodStartedAt.description: Moment the clock for the current period was started.

periodOffsetSeconds.description: Running clock: seconds already on the clock at the start of the period (2700 for the second half in football). Null at a break, when no period is being played. Unit: seconds.

periodEndSeconds.description: Running clock: clock reading, in seconds, at which regulation time for the period runs out (2700 for the first half in football). Null at a break. Unit: seconds.

maxExtraSeconds.description: Running clock: upper bound on the added time the source’s display permits after periodEndSeconds. Null at a break. Unit: seconds.

injuryTimeMinutes.description: Stoppage time announced for the current period; null at a break. Fixture.addedTime keeps the announced minutes of every period. Unit: minutes.

playedSeconds.description: Stop clock: time played in seconds, valid at `playedAt`. When the source's clock jumps forward by up to a minute (handball often runs 15–30 s ahead after a quiet spell), the new reading is used at once since 2026-11-26. A bigger jump, or a reading more than a minute behind (a source that falls back to the previous period at a break), only counts once the next reading agrees, so the clock does not leap about. Unit: seconds.

running.description: Stop clock: true while the game clock is ticking.

runningUpdatedAt.description: Time of the most recent change to `running`.

periodLengthSeconds.description: Stop clock: duration of a single regulation period. Unit: seconds.

overtimeLengthSeconds.description: Duration of a single overtime period. Unit: seconds.

periodCount.description: How many regulation periods the match has (in combat sports, the scheduled rounds).

lastPeriodEndedAt.description: End time of the latest completed period. During a break (half-time, between periods) this marks when the break started, so the break has lasted now − lastPeriodEndedAt. Used with football-style running clocks; null if the source sends nothing (before the first break, in other sports, or for data stored before 2026-11-04). Available since 2026-11-04.

FightResult.description: MMA / boxing: the way a completed fight was settled.

round.description: Round in which the fight finished.

roundTimeSeconds.description: Elapsed time in that round when the fight was halted (KO, TKO, submission, disqualification, …), if the source records it. Null for every decision (unanimous, split, majority, technical, drawn ones too): nothing stopped the fight, and the source’s figure cannot be trusted there. Unit: seconds.

Referee.description: The match official (for cricket, the match referee) and the career totals the source records for them. For a per-match rate, divide a total by `games`.

name.description: Name of the referee.

country.description: Country of the referee, if the source supplies it.

games.description: Number of matches the source has logged with this referee in charge, across the whole career and all competitions.

yellowCards.description: Yellow cards issued across those matches. Null in sports that have no cards (cricket).

redCards.description: Direct red cards issued across those matches. Null in sports that have no cards.

yellowRedCards.description: Dismissals for a second yellow across those matches. Null in sports that have no cards.

image.description: Referee photo hosted on our CDN. Null if no image exists or it has not been uploaded yet. Available since 2026-11-04.

Surface.description: Tennis: the type of court used for the match.

indoor.description: True for an indoor court and false for an outdoor one; null if the source does not specify.

name.description: Surface label as worded by the source, such as "Hardcourt outdoor". For display only.

CricketToss.description: Cricket: outcome of the coin toss.

winner.description: Toss winner; null if the team the source names matches neither participant.

decision.description: The choice the toss winner made.

FightCard.description: MMA / boxing: a bout’s placement on the event card.

section.description: The part of the card (main card, prelims, …), if the source specifies it.

order.description: Position of the bout in the source’s numbering of the card; larger numbers come later, and the main event carries the largest.

weightClass.description: Weight class of the bout, using the source’s naming ("light", "bantam", "feather", …).

FixturePatch.description: Contents of `changes` in a WebSocket delta: a partial Fixture that keeps the same field names and nesting. Deep-merge it into your local Fixture — nested objects merge key by key, while any other value (null included) overwrites. No fields beyond those listed here are ever sent.

status.description: Status fields that were modified. A status change always repeats type, phase and finish, plus period when it is known.

startTime.description: Updated start time, either because the fixture was rescheduled or because the source has logged the actual kick-off (see Fixture.startTime).

winner.description: Sent once the match is over.

homeScore.description: Modified fields of the home ScoreSide.

awayScore.description: Modified fields of the away ScoreSide.

clock.description: Since 2026-11-14 the whole Clock (every field, null where there is no value) is sent whenever any part of it changes. Since 2026-11-26 periodCount, periodLengthSeconds and overtimeLengthSeconds are filled in from the fixture's REST data when the live row lacks them, instead of arriving as null; when that data is at the same status, the period offset, end and added-time fields are filled the same way. Deep-merging it gives the same result as before, and a client that held no clock now receives a complete one. Since 2026-11-26 a delta sent during a break (half-time, an intermission) has periodOffsetSeconds, periodEndSeconds, maxExtraSeconds and injuryTimeMinutes set to null, as REST always had them; until then the WebSocket copy could hold on to the finished period's values. A null value signals the match has ended; discard the clock.

firstToServe.description: Deprecated; carries the same value as `serving`.

servedFirst.description: Darts: which side opened the match, sent as soon as the source provides it. Since 2026-11-11.

battingSide.description: Cricket: side currently batting; null when nobody is.

inningState.description: Baseball: updated game state, always delivered as a complete object; null once play has stopped.

timeouts.description: Basketball and American football: whichever timeout fields changed. `active` comes whole when a timeout starts and as null when play restarts (since 2026-11-21). Null once play has stopped.

downAndDistance.description: American football: fields that were modified (the full object when tracking begins); null once play has stopped. Available since 2026-11-09.

varCheck.description: Football: a full object when a VAR review begins, null when it finishes. Available since 2026-11-09.

durations.description: A newly finished period with its length in seconds (keyed as in ScoreSide.periods; null means the source removed it, so delete it), together with the updated total. Merge it the same way as a score map.

addedTime.description: Only the periods whose announced added time changed, in minutes; a null value means the source took that figure back, so remove the period. Merge it as you would a score map. Since 2026-11-26.

fightResult.description: MMA / boxing: how, in which round and when the fight finished, sent as a whole object once the source has it. Expect it in a delta after the one that ends the fight, since the source releases it ~20–60 s after the winner is known.

homeMembers.description: Tennis doubles and padel: the players of the home pair, always sent as the complete list once anything in it changes. The final result can complete a pair or swap its order, and the delta carrying that result includes them, so merged deltas match a fresh REST read. Available since 2026-11-25.

awayMembers.description: The players of the away pair; see homeMembers. Available since 2026-11-25.

lineupsAvailable.description: True when lineups are published and false when they are pulled, sent as soon as the source announces it, including before kick-off (fixture:{id}). Available since 2026-11-04.

lineupsConfirmed.description: Signals that the official lineups have been released. Available since 2026-11-04.

ScoreSidePatch.description: Only the ScoreSide fields that changed.

current.description: The headline score you would see on a scoreboard: goals, points, sets won (tennis / volleyball) or runs (cricket, baseball), counting extra time / overtime. Shoot-out goals are excluded and reported in `penalties` instead — except in ice hockey and, since 2026-11-23, floorball, where the shoot-out winner is given one extra goal (3-3 after overtime becomes 3-4). Before the start, and for fixtures whose coverage was canceled, it is null.

normalTime.description: Score when regulation time ended, if the source provides it.

penalties.description: Goals converted in a penalty shoot-out. In ice hockey and floorball the shoot-out winner gets 1 here and the loser 0, in line with the single goal added to `current`.

aggregated.description: Combined score across both legs of a two-legged tie.

series.description: Playoff series: number of games this side has won in the series to date (basketball, baseball, ice hockey, water polo).

point.description: Tennis: score within the current game — "0" | "15" | "30" | "40" | "A", or a plain number ("0"–"N") during a tie-break. Darts: the points the side still has to score in the current leg ("501" when a leg starts). Null when play is neither in progress nor interrupted.

redCards.description: Football: number of red cards this side has received, counting second yellows. Once the match is under way it starts at 0 rather than null, on REST and, since 2026-11-26, in WebSocket deltas as well.

hits.description: Baseball: hit total, i.e. the H in the R/H/E line.

errors.description: Baseball: error total, i.e. the E in the R/H/E line.

periods.description: Just the periods whose value changed. A null value means the source removed that period, so delete it.

tieBreaks.description: Just the tie-breaks whose value changed; null means one was removed.

innings.description: Just the innings that changed. Merge them key by key, as with periods; any innings left out keeps its previous value.

TeamRef.description: Compact team reference embedded in other objects (fixtures, standings, players, leaders).

name.description: Name of the team. Individual sports (tennis, table tennis, darts, MMA, …) also model each competitor as a team — a single player, or a doubles pair.

shortName.description: Abbreviated display name, if the source provides one.

code.description: Abbreviation of 1–4 characters as used on scoreboards (e.g. "ARS", "LA"); generated artificially for individual sports.

image.description: Team logo hosted on our CDN; null if the team has no image.

name.description: Name of the team. Individual sports (tennis, table tennis, darts, MMA, …) also model each competitor as a team — a single player, or a doubles pair.

shortName.description: Abbreviated display name, if the source provides one.

code.description: Abbreviation of 1–4 characters as used on scoreboards (e.g. "ARS", "LA"); generated artificially for individual sports.

image.description: Team logo hosted on our CDN; null if the team has no image.

country.description: Country the team is based in or represents.

members.description: Set for doubles teams only (kind `pair`, as in padel or tennis doubles), listing the two people who form the pair; each is a competitor with a profile of their own. Null for every other kind of team. Available since 2026-11-25.

fullName.description: The complete name, when the source keeps one next to the short form used as `name`. Mostly single competitors written "Surname, Given name": table tennis ("Neborak, Dmytro" against "Neborak D.") and snooker. Null otherwise. Available since 2026-11-25.

colors.description: Kit colours in #rrggbb form. Null when the source has no real colours for the team (the source fills in a placeholder blue for every individual competitor and most minor teams).

gender.description: Whether the team is men’s, women’s or mixed; null if the source does not specify.

national.description: True for a national team, false for a club; null if the source does not specify.

kind.description: Distinguishes a team, a single competitor in an individual sport and a doubles pair; null if the source does not specify.

manager.description: Current manager or head coach, if the source names one.

person.description: For individual competitors the source profiles (tennis, MMA): date of birth, height, weight and so on. Null for everyone else.

record.description: MMA / boxing fighters: career win-draw-loss record together with how their most recent fights ended. Null for all other teams.

foundedOn.description: Founding date of the club, if the source has it (roughly half of the teams we have read); null otherwise. Available since 2026-11-09.

motorsport.description: For motorsport drivers and constructors (Formula 1 and others): race number, constructor, chassis and power unit. Null on every other team. Available since 2026-11-20.

currentTeam.description: For an individual competitor: the team they compete for today, such as a cyclist’s trade team or a racing driver’s constructor (which motorsport.constructor also gives). Teams themselves, and competitors with no team, read null. Available since 2026-11-24.

activePeriods.description: Spans of years in which the team competed, where the source records them (Formula 1 constructors, for example); [] for most teams. Available since 2026-11-21.

Person.description: Personal details of an individual competitor (`kind: individual`) for whom the source keeps a profile (tennis players, MMA fighters). Field names and units match Player.

weightKg.description: Body weight in kilograms (for MMA, the weight the fighter is listed at).

reachCm.description: Arm reach, for MMA. Unit: cm.

nickname.description: MMA ring name or nickname, such as "Storm".

weightClass.description: Weight class in the source’s wording (MMA: "feather", "light", "bantam", …).

birthplace.description: Place of birth in the source’s wording ("San Candido, Italy").

residence.description: Place of residence in the source’s wording ("Monte Carlo, Monaco").

handedness.description: Tennis: which hand the player plays with.

turnedPro.description: Tennis: year the player became a professional.

prizeMoneySeason.description: Tennis: prize money earned in the current season.

prizeMoneyCareer.description: Tennis: total prize money earned over the career.

fightingStyle.description: MMA: the fighter’s style in the source’s own word ("mma", …); null in other sports and when it is not given. Available since 2026-11-23.

underage.description: The source's junior marker: true for a competitor it lists as under age, false when it states the opposite, null when it is silent. Available since 2026-11-27.

LeagueRef.description: A league or competition. /v2/leagues/{id} and every league list return this same shape.

name.description: Name of the league or competition.

sport.description: Slug of the sport, matching the values listed by /v2/sports.

category.description: How the source groups the league: by country ("England"), region ("International", "North America", "World"), tour ("ATP", "WTA") or game (esports: "Counter Strike"). It is not necessarily a country; use `country` for that.

country.description: Country of the league when its category is a country. Since 2026-11-25 a competition filed under a region can still carry its own home country where the source records one, as MMA promotions do (the UFC and PFL are American, ONE is based in Singapore). Otherwise null, as for the remaining regions, tours and games.

image.description: League logo hosted on our CDN; null if the league has no image.

priority.description: The source’s prominence ranking for the competition, handy for ordering leagues: a higher value means a bigger competition (for example 719 for the Champions League, 704 for the Premier League, 702 for LaLiga, 519 for Primeira Liga), and 0 means unranked. It is filled only where the source supplies it: on the league embedded in a fixture and in the /v2/fixtures?date&sport day lists. Everywhere else — league profiles, directories, search — it is null, as it is on rows saved before 2026-11-04. Available since 2026-11-04.

code.description: Two-letter code supplied by the source. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, apart from XK for Kosovo and four codes for the UK home nations (England EN, Scotland SX, Wales WA, Northern Ireland NX). Null if unknown.

name.description: Country name in English.

flag.description: Flag image (PNG) hosted on our CDN. Null when there is no code or the image has not been uploaded yet. Available since 2026-11-04.

name.description: Full season name, such as "Premier League 26/27".

year.description: Display label in the source’s format: "26/27" or "2026/2027" when the season spans two years, "2026" for a calendar-year season. Use startYear / endYear for sorting and filtering.

startYear.description: Year in which the season begins (2026 for both "26/27" and "2026"); null if the label cannot be parsed.

endYear.description: Year in which the season finishes (2027 for "26/27"; equal to startYear for a calendar-year season); null if the label cannot be parsed.

Round.description: One round within a league season.

number.description: Round number from the source. Treat it as an opaque key rather than a sequence: cups count rounds by how many entrants remain (32 for a tennis "Round of 64"), and playoff rounds get large values (636). Use it with /v2/leagues/{id}/fixtures. The source gives some competitions no round structure — NBA and NHL regular seasons, NCAA, one-off tennis or MMA events; their fixtures may still have a round, but /rounds comes back empty and filtering by round yields nothing, so query them by date.

name.description: Name of the round, if it has one ("Quarterfinals", "Playoff round").

slug.description: Tells apart rounds that share a number across different phases. When present, include it in /fixtures requests.

prefix.description: An additional qualifier (e.g. "Qualification"); send it to /fixtures along with slug.

Rounds.description: All rounds of a season plus the one in progress. Returned empty (`current: null`, `rounds: []`) for competitions the source does not structure in rounds; see Round.number.

Venue.description: A stadium or arena: where a fixture takes place, or a team’s home ground.

id.description: The venue’s DataSportsAPI id; null if the source supplies the venue without an id.

name.description: Name of the stadium or arena.

city.description: City where the venue is located.

country.description: Country where the venue is located.

PlayerRef.description: Compact player reference embedded in other objects.

name.description: Name of the player.

shortName.description: Abbreviated display name such as "B. Saka", if the source provides one.

image.description: Player photo hosted on our CDN; null if the player has no image.

ManagerRef.description: Compact reference to a team’s manager (head coach), embedded in other objects.

name.description: Name of the manager or head coach.

image.description: Manager photo hosted on our CDN. Null if no image exists or it has not been uploaded yet. Available since 2026-11-04.

name.description: The player’s full name.

firstName.description: Given name from the source's records; handy where `name` is a handle rather than a real name, as in esports. Null when unknown. Available since 2026-11-25.

lastName.description: Family name from the source's records; null when unknown. Available since 2026-11-25.

gender.description: Gender as the source has it on file; null when unknown. Available since 2026-11-25.

rosterStatus.description: The player's standing on the team roster, in leagues where the source tracks one: the NBA (active, two-way contract) and the NHL (active, injured reserve). Null in other leagues. Available since 2026-11-25.

position.description: Primary playing position.

positionCode.description: Position code as used by the source.

jerseyNumber.description: Shirt number as a string, since basketball and American football treat "0" and "00" as distinct numbers. Null if unknown; rugby squads’ "0" placeholder is dropped.

preferredFoot.description: Football: the player’s stronger foot — left, right or both.

country.description: The player’s nationality.

marketValue.description: Estimated value on the transfer market; null if unknown.

contractUntil.description: Date the current contract expires; null if unknown.

image.description: Player photo hosted on our CDN.

injury.description: Ongoing injury, if the source records one (football, mainly in covered leagues); null means no injury is listed.

detailedPositions.description: Football: fine-grained positions the player occupies, primary first (e.g. ["striker"], ["rightWinger", "attackingMidfielder"]). Empty if the source lists none, as in other sports and minor leagues; `position` keeps the broad line either way.

suspensions.description: Football: the bans the player is serving this season, one entry per competition. An empty list means none, or that our data source does not list them. Available since 2026-11-20.

primaryPosition.description: Basketball only: the specific spot the player is listed at — pointGuard, shootingGuard, smallForward, powerForward or center (PG / SG / SF / PF / C at the source); `position` stays the broader guard, forward or center group. Null in other sports, when the source gives no code, and for a player stored earlier until his next refresh. Available since 2026-11-25.

team.description: Team the player currently belongs to.

battingHand.description: Cricket and baseball: the side the player bats from; switch marks a baseball switch hitter, who bats from both. Null in other sports and when unknown. Available since 2026-11-23.

throwingHand.description: Baseball: left- or right-handed thrower; null in other sports and when unknown. Available since 2026-11-23.

bowlingStyle.description: Cricket: how the player bowls, in the source’s words ("Right-arm fast"); null in other sports and for players who do not bowl. Available since 2026-11-23.

weightKg.description: Body weight where the source records it (baseball, American football and a few more). Unit: kg. Available since 2026-11-23.

birthPlace.description: Birthplace in the source’s words ("Maracaibo, Venezuela"); null if not known. Available since 2026-11-23.

salary.description: Yearly salary, where the source carries one (mostly MLB players); null otherwise. Available since 2026-11-23.

deceased.description: true when the source records the player as deceased; null when it says nothing. Available since 2026-11-24.

Injury.description: An injury a player is currently carrying.

description.description: Name of the injury, such as "Hamstring Injury".

status.description: Availability status: out, day to day, …

expectedReturn.description: Projected return date (UTC day), if the source offers an estimate.

updatedAt.description: Time of the source’s latest update to this injury.

SquadPlayer.description: A member of a squad. Identical to Player minus `team`, which is implied by the squad.

name.description: The player’s full name.

firstName.description: Given name from the source's records; handy where `name` is a handle rather than a real name, as in esports. Null when unknown. Available since 2026-11-25.

lastName.description: Family name from the source's records; null when unknown. Available since 2026-11-25.

gender.description: Gender as the source has it on file; null when unknown. Available since 2026-11-25.

positionCode.description: Position code as used by the source.

country.description: The player’s nationality.

image.description: Player photo hosted on our CDN.

injury.description: Ongoing injury, if the source records one (football, mainly in covered leagues); null means no injury is listed.

suspensions.description: Football: the bans the player is serving this season, one entry per competition. An empty list means none, or that our data source does not list them. Available since 2026-11-20.

Null in other sports, when the source gives no code, and for a player stored earlier until his next refresh. Available since 2026-11-25.

battingHand.description: Cricket and baseball: the side the player bats from; switch marks a baseball switch hitter, who bats from both. Null in other sports and when unknown. Available since 2026-11-23.

throwingHand.description: Baseball: left- or right-handed thrower; null in other sports and when unknown. Available since 2026-11-23.

bowlingStyle.description: Cricket: how the player bowls, in the source’s words ("Right-arm fast"); null in other sports and for players who do not bowl. Available since 2026-11-23.

weightKg.description: Body weight where the source records it (baseball, American football and a few more). Unit: kg. Available since 2026-11-23.

birthPlace.description: Birthplace in the source’s words ("Maracaibo, Venezuela"); null if not known. Available since 2026-11-23.

salary.description: Yearly salary, where the source carries one (mostly MLB players); null otherwise. Available since 2026-11-23.

deceased.description: true when the source records the player as deceased; null when it says nothing. Available since 2026-11-24.

previousTeam.description: For a player who joined recently, his previous team, if the source records the move (mostly on NFL rosters); null in all other cases. Available since 2026-11-23.

joinedOn.description: Date of the player’s arrival at this team (a signing, a trade, a call-up), where the source records it; null otherwise. Available since 2026-11-23.

club.description: The player’s own team when it differs from the squad you asked for: on a national squad, the club or domestic side he plays for (for cricket, a state or county side). It stays null when you read a club’s squad, when no team is given, and on squads stored before 2026-11-27 until their next refresh. Since 2026-11-27.

DepthChartEntry.description: A single slot on a team’s depth chart and the player who fills it. Someone who holds two slots shows up twice — a top-line centre frequently skates on a power-play unit as well. Available since 2026-11-23.

position.description: The slot: a wing or centre of a forward line, one side of a defence pair, a goaltender, or a power-play unit.

depth.description: Which line, pair or goalie rank the slot belongs to, counting from 1 for the first; for a power-play unit, the player’s place within that unit (1–5).

Transfer.description: A single player movement between teams, such as a transfer, loan, signing, trade or release. It has no id; the combination of player, type and date identifies it.

date.description: Date the move became effective (UTC day); null if the source gives no date.

from.description: Club the player departed; null for a free agent or for a side the source has no team record for (see `fromName`).

fromName.description: The club the player left, named as the source writes it (e.g. "Bryne FK Yth."); set even when `from` is null.

to.description: Club the player moved to; null after a waiver, release or retirement, or for a side the source has no team record for (`toName` then reads "No team" for releases and free agents).

toName.description: Name of the destination club as written by the source; works like `fromName`.

fee.description: Transfer fee, if the source states it. Null for free, undisclosed or unknown fees and for any move that is not a transfer.

freeTransfer.description: True if the source marks the move as free, meaning no fee changed hands.

draft.description: For type draft: the round and pick number, if listed. Null otherwise.

TeamTransfers.description: Recent incoming and outgoing moves for a team as listed by the source, covering roughly the past year.

TransferFeed.description: One page of the most recent football transfers (GET /v2/transfers). Available since 2026-11-09.

transfers.description: Moves on this page (no more than 50), sorted as requested.

hasNextPage.description: True if another page might contain further moves.

amount.description: The value, expressed in units of `currency`.

currency.description: Currency as an ISO 4217 code, such as "EUR".

MoneyChange.description: How much a sum of money went up or down. Available since 2026-11-25.

amount.description: The difference in `currency` units, above zero for an increase and below zero for a decrease.

currency.description: Currency as an ISO 4217 code, such as "EUR".

confirmed.description: True when the official lineups have been released; false means they are predicted or not yet published.

TeamLineup.description: The lineup of a single side.

supportStaff.description: Coaches and other staff named alongside the lineup (in cricket: the head coach plus the batting and bowling coaches). An empty list when the source names none (the usual case outside cricket) and on any lineup stored before 2026-11-18. Available since 2026-11-18.

LineupPlayer.description: An individual entry in a lineup.

position.description: Position the player fills in this lineup.

positionCode.description: Position code from the source, as shown on a team sheet ("G", "LW", "QB", "1B").

jerseyNumber.description: Shirt number as a string, since "00" is possible. Also filled where the source keeps the number only on the player record, as in handball (since 2026-11-23).

substitute.description: True if the player started on the bench.

heightCm.description: Height, copied over from the profile at GET /v2/players/{id}; null if the source has no value. Available since 2026-11-06. Unit: cm.

dateOfBirth.description: Birth date from the player’s profile; null if unknown. Available since 2026-11-06.

country.description: Nationality from the player’s profile, flag included; null if unknown. Available since 2026-11-06.

marketValue.description: Estimated market value from the player’s profile; null if unknown (the source only provides it for some football players). Available since 2026-11-06.

rating.description: Match rating to 2 decimal places (e.g. 7.4); null for an unrated player.

avgRating.description: Football: the player’s average match rating over the season (2 decimals), included when the source sends it with the lineup — usually in the run-up to kick-off and around it.

ratingVersions.description: Football: the rating from the original model alongside the one from the source’s alternative model.

star.description: Ice hockey: whether the player was picked as first, second or third star of the game.

battingOrder.description: Baseball: the player’s slot in the batting order.

statistics.description: The player’s match statistics, using sport-specific camelCase keys from the same vocabulary as team statistics: whenever a key measures the same thing as a team StatItem, it shares that key (football minutesPlayed, passes, accuratePasses, shotsOnGoal, expectedGoals …; basketball points, fieldGoalsMade, fieldGoalsAttempted, secondsPlayed …; ice hockey goals, shotsOnGoal, penalties, plusMinus, savePercentage …). On NBA games played after 2026-11-22 21:00 UTC, a live box score adds `pointsFastBreak`, `pointsInPaint`, `pointsFromTurnovers` and `foulsDrawn` for the players it lists; other leagues lack them. In football matches the live tracker follows (MLS and the Champions League among them), from 2026-11-23 on: `injuries` and `cornerKicks` (corners he took), plus a goalkeeper’s `shotsFaced` (the opposition’s attempts during his time in goal) and `cleanSheet` (1 or 0, judged on the minutes he played; it reads 0 until the match is over), from a live box score supplied by a different provider, for the players it lists. The football penalty keys (penaltyWon, penaltyConceded, penaltyMiss, penaltyFaced, penaltySave) are listed in the data dictionary. Every …Percentage key is a share from 0 to 100 — ice-hockey save percentages too (94.1 rather than 0.941). Values are in seconds where the key name says so. Null if the player has no statistics.

baseballRoles.description: Baseball: each part the player took in the game, in the order he took it. A starter switched from left to centre field reads [leftField, centerField]; a substitute who batted for a team-mate and then stayed on at first base reads [pinchHitter, firstBase]. An empty list outside baseball, or when the source has no record of it. Available since 2026-11-23.

entrySequence.description: Baseball: the order players came into the game, as numbered in the source’s box score. Starters carry the lowest numbers and each substitute follows the moment he entered. Null in other sports. Available since 2026-11-23.

MissingPlayer.description: A player who is unavailable for a fixture.

availability.description: Whether the player is ruled out or only doubtful.

description.description: Further detail in the source’s words, such as "Hamstring Injury" or "Red card suspension".

SupportStaffMember.description: A coach or other staff member named with a side’s lineup.

id.description: DataSportsAPI id for the person, the same in every fixture (no endpoint looks it up); null when the source supplies none.

name.description: The person’s name.

role.description: What the person does; null when the source does not say.

country.description: Nationality, if the source supplies it.

Statistics.description: Match statistics broken down by period.

periods.description: An entry for each period the source provides statistics for, beginning with "all". Overtime is split by overtime period (overtime1, overtime2, …); the single overtime of an NHL regular-season game is overtime1.

key.description: Stable group identifier from a per-sport table, not derived from the display name — "matchOverview", "attack", "other" and so on.

name.description: Human-readable group title, such as "Match overview".

StatItem.description: A single match statistic with values for both teams.

key.description: Stable camelCase identifier. A given key always denotes the same quantity, across all sports and in lineup player statistics, though it may show up in two groups. Ratio keys are named after the successes their `value` counts (`aerialDuelsWon`, `fieldGoalsMade`, `accurateCrosses`, `firstServesIn`, `powerPlayConversion`) and never end in `…Percentage`; that suffix is reserved for keys whose `value` is already a 0–100 share (`duelsWonPercentage`, `corsiPercentage`). Note that `blocks` counts attempts this side blocked, while `shotsBlocked` counts this side’s own shots that got blocked. On NBA games played after 2026-11-22 21:00 UTC, a live box score adds `pointsFastBreak`, `pointsInPaint`, `pointsFromTurnovers`, `foulsDrawn` and `foulsToGive` (fouls a side has left in the period until the other team shoots bonus free throws), in the `all` period only; other leagues lack them. In football matches the live tracker follows (MLS and the Champions League among them), from 2026-11-23 on, a live box score from a different provider adds `injuries` (group matchOverview, `all` period). The data dictionary lists every key per sport.

name.description: English label as provided by the source.

kind.description: Tells you how to interpret the value and total of the statistic.

higherIs.description: Indicates whether a larger number is better; use it to emphasise the side that leads.

StatSide.description: A single team’s value for a statistic.

display.description: Ready-to-display text in the source’s own form, such as "57%", "33/53 (62%)" or "1:22". A ratio keeps the percentage the source prints, which some competitions and statistics round down ("21/49 (42%)") while others round normally; we compute it ourselves (rounded) only where the source’s figure fits neither (table tennis sends "(0%)").

value.description: Underlying numeric value; interpret it using the item’s `kind`.

total.description: For kind ratio, the number of attempts; for kind time, the seconds available. Null for other kinds.

Incident.description: Something that happened during a match. As with all timeline lists, entries run oldest first (chronological order).

detail.description: Sub-category within the type; null on period and injuryTime rows.

side.description: Side the event is credited to (an own goal belongs to the side that benefits from it); null on period / injuryTime rows.

minute.description: Match minute. Null whenever the clock is stopped — before kick-off, at half-time and after full time, for bench events, and during a shoot-out. Unit: minutes.

addedMinute.description: How far into stoppage time the event happened (90+3 gives minute 90, addedMinute 3). On injuryTime rows it holds the announced minutes. Unit: minutes.

second.description: Game clock in seconds, if the source supplies it — present on all rows in ice hockey, basketball, handball and rugby, but only on period rows in football. Unit: seconds.

period.description: Period in which the event took place. On period rows it is the period that just ended (ET → extra2, PEN → penalties, FT → period2 in football and period4 in basketball). On other rows it is the period bounded by the surrounding period rows, or the source’s own value when supplied; shoot-out kicks use penalties. A card shown to the bench takes the period its `benchMinute` falls in (since 2026-11-26). Null only if it cannot be determined (no period row yet and the period length for the sport is unknown).

player.description: Main player involved: the scorer, the booked or penalised player, the subject of a VAR check, or the shoot-out taker.

playerName.description: Name of the player; filled even when the source provides a name without a player record (as with some own goals). For a card given to a manager it is the manager's name.

manager.description: Set when the incident concerns a manager (head coach) on the bench, such as a booking from the touchline: our id for that manager. Null on every other row. Available since 2026-11-26.

benchMinute.description: For an incident on the bench, which the match clock does not count (a manager's card): the minute of play it came in, in the source's count. `minute` is null on such rows, and `period` follows from this minute (a booking in the 63rd minute is in period2). Null otherwise. Available since 2026-11-26. Unit: minutes.

assists.description: Players credited with assists on the goal who have a player record, in order (up to two in ice hockey). An assister the source names without a record appears only in assistNames.

assistNames.description: Every assist on the goal as a name, in order, including assisters the source names without a player record (frequent in futsal, where assists could stay empty). Incidents stored before 2026-11-24 read [] until they are refreshed. Available since 2026-11-24.

bodyPart.description: Football goals only: `head` when the source's event list marks the goal as a header (only some leagues do, and they never name a foot); null on every other goal and incident. The goal's `buildUp` and the shotmap carry the body part more often. Available since 2026-11-23.

playerIn.description: For a substitution: the player entering the field.

playerOut.description: For a substitution: the player leaving the field.

injury.description: On a substitution, `true` if the player left the pitch injured; null on every other incident and when our data source does not say. Available since 2026-11-20.

drawnBy.description: For an ice hockey suspension: the player who drew the penalty.

servedBy.description: For an ice hockey suspension: the player who sat in the penalty box in place of the penalised player (for a goalkeeper’s penalty or a bench minor, say). Null when the penalised player served it, and in every other sport. Available since 2026-11-18.

infraction.description: For an ice hockey suspension: the offence under a camelCase key that does not change ("tripping", "interference", "crossChecking", "slashing", "roughing"), or "minor" if the source does not name one, with `reason` holding the same thing as display text. Expect new keys over time. Null in other sports. Available since 2026-11-18.

severity.description: For an ice hockey suspension: the class of penalty (minor, major, …); null if the source leaves it out, and always null outside ice hockey. Available since 2026-11-18.

seasonGoals.description: For an ice hockey goal, where the source keeps the count (NHL): the scorer’s goals so far this season, this one included — the number a scoresheet prints in brackets after the name, as in "(12)". Null otherwise. Available since 2026-11-18.

seasonAssists.description: For an ice hockey goal (NHL): each assisting player’s assists so far this season, this one included — one entry for each entry of `assists`, in the same order, and null for a player the source has no count for. An empty list when the source keeps no counts. Available since 2026-11-18.

homeScore.description: Home score immediately after the event (on goals, period rows and shoot-out kicks). For period rows in set sports (volleyball, table tennis, badminton) it is the number of sets won so far; the points inside each set are given by /points and by the fixture’s `periods`.

awayScore.description: Away score immediately after the event (sets won, on period rows in set sports).

text.description: On period rows: the label a scoreboard would show ("HT", "FT", "Q4", "3rd period", "Overtime", "PEN"). For display only.

reason.description: For a card, why it was shown ("Foul", "Violent conduct"); for a suspension, the offence ("Holding"); for a missed penalty, how it was missed ("Goalkeeper save", "Off target").

rescinded.description: For a card: true if it was later withdrawn.

confirmed.description: For a varDecision: true when the original decision was upheld.

shootoutSequence.description: For a shootoutPenalty: position of the kick in the overall order across both teams (1 is the opening kick of the shoot-out).

shootoutRound.description: For a shootoutPenalty: the round, i.e. whether it was the taking side’s 1st, 2nd, … kick.

durationSeconds.description: For a suspension: how long the player is excluded. Unit: seconds.

buildUp.description: For a football goal: the sequence of passes and shots leading up to it, ending with the goal itself (covered leagues only; empty elsewhere and for all other incidents).

KeyedIncident.description: An incident paired with its stable key, as used in events frames.

key.description: Identifier of the incident that stays stable within the fixture, built as `type:side:minute:addedMinute` (e.g. "goal:home:34:0", with "-" standing in for a null side or minute). Additional incidents in the same slot get `#2`, `#3`, … in list order. The player is not part of the key, so correcting the scorer or goal type keeps the key and counts as an update; correcting the minute produces a new key and removes the old one.

incident.description: The match event itself. As with all timeline lists, entries run oldest first (chronological order).

IncidentChanges.description: The difference between an events frame and the one before it.

added.description: Keys of incidents that did not exist in the previous events frame (or in the server’s earlier copy).

updated.description: Keys of incidents whose details were modified (scorer, assist, build-up, rescinded card, …).

removed.description: Incidents that have disappeared from the source, each with its final content — for example a goal cancelled by VAR. The score reverts through a delta, and the goal shows up here once REST confirms its removal.

BuildUpStep.description: A single action in the move leading to a goal, as mapped by the source (football, covered leagues).

action.description: Type of action performed in this step.

side.description: Team of the player performing the action (for an own goal, the final step belongs to the defending side).

minute.description: Minute of the match. Unit: minutes.

position.description: Pitch location where the action began.

endPosition.description: For a pass / cross: where the ball ended up. Null for other actions.

assist.description: True for the pass credited as the assist.

bodyPart.description: For the goal: the body part used to strike it.

expectedGoals.description: For a goal / savedShot: xG value of the chance on a 0–1 scale, if the source provides it.

expectedGoalsOnTarget.description: For a goal / savedShot: expected goals on target (xGOT), if available.

goalMouthLocation.description: For the goal: the area of the goal mouth it went into.

PitchSpot.description: A location on a football pitch.

x.description: Lengthwise position from 0 to 100, oriented in the attacking direction of the SCORING side (100 is the goal the ball ended up in, own goals included). For away goals we rotate the source’s coordinates, in which the home side always attacks towards 100 (corrected 2026-10-23). Unit: percent.

y.description: Widthwise position from 0 to 100, rotated together with x (seen from the scoring side). Unit: percent.

H2H.description: The record of the two teams against each other; the endpoint answers null when there is none.

homeWins.description: Meetings won by the home team of this fixture.

awayWins.description: Meetings won by the away team of this fixture.

managerDuel.description: How the two managers have fared head to head (football and other sports that have managers). Null if they have never met or the source has no data.

ManagerDuel.description: Head-to-head record between the two managers, counting every team either of them has managed. Only the counts are given; the managers themselves come from /v2/fixtures/{id}/managers.

homeWins.description: Wins for teams led by the home manager over teams led by the away manager.

awayWins.description: Wins for the away manager’s teams.

MatchManagers.description: The managers (head coaches) in charge of one particular match, kept as they were on the day even long afterwards. Fixture.homeManager / awayManager, by contrast, show each team’s current manager. Both are null when the source names no manager, as in most sports that have none.

homeManager.description: Manager of the home side in this match; null if the source names none.

awayManager.description: Manager of the away side in this match; works like homeManager.

PregameForm.description: Form of both sides heading into a fixture, within its competition. A side is null if the source has no form for it — tennis, for instance, for which the source has no competition form guide. The latest matches of each side across every competition are on /v2/fixtures/{id}/team-form.

TeamForm.description: Pre-match form of a single side.

results.description: Up to five most recent results in this competition prior to the fixture, ordered from oldest to newest.

position.description: Table position before the fixture.

points.description: Points in the table before the fixture, for competitions whose standings use points (football, ice hockey, handball, rugby, …); null otherwise.

wins.description: Wins going into the fixture, for tables that count wins and losses instead of points (W-L in basketball and baseball, W-D-L in MMA); null otherwise. In MMA it is the source’s tally inside the event’s competition — e.g. Volkanovski at 8-0-3 ahead of UFC 333, with a 28-0-4 career record — not the career record — that lives in TeamDetail.record on /v2/teams/{id}.

draws.description: Draws, for records that include them (MMA W-D-L); null otherwise.

avgRating.description: Average player rating of the side over its recent matches (2 decimals).

FormFixture.description: A recent match played by a side ahead of a fixture, including its score (from /v2/fixtures/{id}/team-form).

league.description: Competition the match belonged to, of any type (league, cup, European, friendly).

side.description: Whether the team was home or away in that match.

scoreFor.description: Score the team achieved, equal to its side’s Fixture score `current` (goals, points; sets in tennis).

result.description: Outcome for the team as interpreted by the source; matches settled in overtime or on penalties count as a win for the side that prevailed.

TeamFormFixtures.description: The latest matches of each side before a fixture, across every competition, each with opponent, score and result. Filled for tennis as well, where the competition form guide (/v2/fixtures/{id}/form) has nothing.

home.description: Up to five finished matches the home side played in ANY competition before this fixture, ordered oldest to newest; empty if the source has none.

away.description: The same list for the away side.

Streaks.description: Runs of form for both teams heading into a fixture.

general.description: For both sides, the streaks that run through their latest matches in every competition before this fixture. After the final whistle it keeps the streaks the match was played with.

headToHead.description: Streaks drawn from matches between the two sides.

Streak.description: A noteworthy team streak to highlight before a fixture.

name.description: English description of the streak, such as "Wins", "No losses" or "More than 2.5 goals". Display text only, since the source provides no stable key.

kind.description: How to read the figure: an average, a consecutive run, or x out of the last y.

value.description: The figure exactly as the source formats it: "5" for five in a row, "7/8" when seven of the last eight qualified, "83" for an average.

count.description: Number of matches for which the streak holds (the 5 in "5", the 7 in "7/8"); null for an average.

outOf.description: The y in an "x of the last y" streak; null for consecutive runs and averages.

average.description: For kind average, the value itself (83 points a game); null otherwise.

side.description: Which team the streak belongs to.

continued.description: True if the streak is still active.

playerOfTheMatch.description: The player of the match, in sports that award one.

leaderboard.description: One ranking of the match across both teams, best first, where the source keeps one: handball’s ten leading scorers, basketball by points, every baseball top performer. home and away then list only each team’s best. [] when the source ranks none. Available since 2026-11-23.

BestPlayer.description: One of the standout players in a match.

value.description: Figure the ranking is based on (a rating, points, goals, yards). Baseball (since 2026-11-23): a top-performer score from the source with label rating, higher meaning better; the source publishes no scale for it.

statistics.description: Basketball: the player’s stat line, using the same keys as lineup statistics (points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, rating). For baseball, available since 2026-11-04, the numbers — pitching or batting — that got the player picked (pitchingInningsPitched, pitchingStrikeOuts, battingHits, battingHomeRuns, battingRbi, …). Null in any sport where the source lists nothing.

role.description: Baseball (since 2026-11-04): pitcher or batter, i.e. the role the player was picked for; null for every other sport.

RankedBestPlayer.description: A place on a match’s leaderboard (BestPlayers.leaderboard): the fields of a BestPlayer plus the team the player was on. Available since 2026-11-23.

value.description: The figure the place rests on: a rating, points, goals or yards; in baseball the source’s top-performer rating.

statistics.description: Basketball and baseball: the player’s line, in the keys of lineup statistics; null where the source lists none.

role.description: Baseball: whether he made the list as a pitcher or as a batter; null in other sports.

side.description: His club at the time; null if the source's row leaves it out.
