Momentum.description: Values for drawing a momentum chart: one per game in tennis, one per minute in football, basketball, handball, ice hockey and the like.

points.description: One value for every minute, in match order; points in added time come after the final minute of their period.

periodLengthMinutes.description: How long one regulation period lasts — 45 minutes in football, 10 in basketball, 20 in ice hockey. Unit: minutes.

overtimeLengthMinutes.description: Duration of a single overtime period. Unit: minutes.

overtimeCount.description: How many overtime periods were played, if the source reports it.

games.description: Tennis: a value for each game in sequence (minute points stay empty). Empty in other sports.

Shot.description: A single shot attempt (football, ice hockey, basketball field goals). Lists run chronologically, oldest first, with shoot-out kicks at the end in kick order. Basketball is the exception: the source gives no timing, so one team’s shots (team=home|away) arrive in whatever order the source lists them, and side, outcome and position are the only fields filled.

goalType.description: Set on goals only: regular, ownGoal or penalty.

situation.description: Football: the phase of play that produced the shot.

bodyPart.description: Football: body part used to strike the ball.

strength.description: Ice hockey: the manpower situation at the time.

expectedGoals.description: xG value of the chance on a 0–1 scale.

expectedGoalsOnTarget.description: Football: post-shot expected goals (xGOT), set for shots on target.

minute.description: Minute of the match. Unit: minutes.

addedMinute.description: How far into stoppage time the shot came. Unit: minutes.

second.description: Game clock reading in seconds. Unit: seconds.

period.description: Period in which the shot came. In football the minute decides it (shoot-out kicks → penalties, 45+2 → period1, 92 → extra1); in ice hockey it is the source’s period (overtime1 for a shot in overtime); basketball has no timing, so it stays null.

position.description: Where the shot was taken from. Football: pitch percentages 0–100, with x measured from the goal line under attack and y across the pitch. Ice hockey: x roughly 0–240 along the ice (rink units from the source, each side attacking one end) and y covering 0–100 from side to side. Basketball: tenths of a foot measured from the basket being attacked; x runs across the court (−250…250 sideline to sideline), y away from the basket (0 is the rim, and the NBA three-point arc sits at 237.5).

goalMouth.description: Football: point at which the ball crossed the goal line (y 0–100 across the goal mouth, z for height).

goalMouthLocation.description: Football: zone of the goal mouth the shot reached, or of the near miss.

blockPosition.description: Football: the point at which a blocked or saved shot was halted.

shootoutSequence.description: Football shoot-out kicks: where the kick falls in the combined order of both teams (the same numbering the shoot-out incidents use).

shootoutRound.description: Football shoot-out kicks: which of the shooting side’s kicks this was (1st, 2nd, …).

Point.description: A coordinate pair; see Shot for each sport’s coordinate system.

Heatmap.description: Activity map of one player across a fixture (football, covered leagues).

points.description: All recorded samples, meant to be drawn as a density map. If the source has no heatmap for this player and fixture — always so outside football — the list comes back empty with 200, not 404.

HeatPoint.description: A single touch or position sample within a heatmap.

x.description: Lengthwise position from 0 to 100, oriented in the player’s attacking direction (100 is the goal being attacked). Unit: percent.

y.description: Widthwise position from 0 to 100. Unit: percent.

AveragePositions.description: Mean on-pitch positions of every player on both sides (football, covered leagues).

AveragePosition.description: Where a player was positioned on average during a fixture.

position.description: Position as used in lineups, derived from `positionCode`.

positionCode.description: Single-letter position code from the source ("G", "D", "M", "F").

x.description: Mean lengthwise position from 0 to 100, oriented in the team’s attacking direction. Unit: percent.

y.description: Mean widthwise position from 0 to 100. Unit: percent.

pointsCount.description: Number of position samples the average is computed from.

Points.description: A fixture’s point-by-point record, shaped by sport: sets → games → points in tennis, sets → rallies in rally sports, innings → overs → balls in cricket, at-bats in baseball, and sets → legs → visits in darts.

format.description: Names the list among `sets` / `innings` / `atBats` / `darts` that has data. Null until something arrives, and in sports without any point-by-point data — those get 200 with empty lists rather than 404.

sets.description: Tennis and rally sports: an entry for each set, in sequence.

innings.description: Cricket: an entry for each innings, in sequence.

atBats.description: Baseball: all plate appearances in chronological order, oldest first.

darts.description: Darts: nested sets → legs → visits, in sequence.

PointSet.description: Point-by-point detail of a single set.

period.description: Which set this is: period1, period2, …

homeScore.description: Games (tennis) or points (rally sports) the home side won in the set, taken from the final listed score. For a tennis match tie-break the points are counted (10-8), consistent with the fixture’s period score.

awayScore.description: Games / points the away side won in the set.

games.description: Tennis: each game in sequence. Empty for rally sports.

points.description: Rally sports: each rally in sequence as recorded by the source. Lower-tier coverage may skip a rally, which shows up as a jump in the running score. Empty for tennis.

TennisGame.description: A single game within a tennis set.

number.description: Position of the game in the set (13 is the tie-break). When a match tie-break stands in for the deciding set, it is that set’s game 1, played to 10 points.

server.description: The serving side. For a tie-break the source reports whoever served its LAST point rather than its first (verified against real tie-breaks on 2026-10-19).

winner.description: Side that took the game; if it differs from the server, serve was broken. For a completed tie-break we take the winner from its final point, because in a check on 2026-10-19 the source had the wrong game winner on 3 of 8 match tie-breaks.

homeGames.description: Games won by the home side in the set once this game is over.

awayGames.description: Games won by the away side in the set once this game is over.

points.description: Each point in sequence. For a completed game the final point is the one that decided it (its `winner` matches the game’s winner); for a game still under way, the points played so far.

TennisPoint.description: A single point within a tennis game.

homeScore.description: Home side’s game score following the point: "0", "15", "30", "40", "A" (plain numbers in a tie-break). It is a string to accommodate "A". Null on the point that closes a regular game, since no score exists once the game is over.

awayScore.description: Away side’s game score following the point; null in the same case as `homeScore`.

winner.description: Side that won the point, inferred from how the score changed; null if that cannot be inferred.

description.description: Marks an ace or a double fault; null for all other points and for the game-winning point we append. The source does not list that final point, so an ace that closes a game goes unmarked.

homeType.description: What the point means for the home side (point won, now holding break or set point, mini-break in a tie-break). Null on the game-winning point added at the end.

awayType.description: Significance of the point for the away side, as for homeType.

RallyPoint.description: A single rally within a set (volleyball, table tennis, badminton).

homeScore.description: Home side’s points in the set following the rally.

awayScore.description: Away side’s points in the set following the rally.

InningsBalls.description: Ball-by-ball record of a single cricket innings.

battingSide.description: Side at bat during this innings.

Over.description: A single over within an innings.

number.description: Over number, starting at 1 for the opening over. Cricket notation counts completed overs instead, so the 3rd ball of over 46 reads "45.3".

sequence.description: Running delivery counter from the source across the whole match, useful for ordering deliveries between overs.

ball.description: Delivery number inside the over; extras can take it above 6.

totalRuns.description: All runs the delivery contributed, extras included.

wicket.description: True if a wicket fell on this ball.

dismissal.description: Manner of dismissal, when a wicket fell.

fielder.description: Fielder who took part in a dismissal (catch, run-out, stumping).

dismissedBatter.description: Batter who was dismissed, which is not always the striker (run-outs).

scoreRuns.description: Batting side’s total runs once the delivery is complete.

scoreWickets.description: Wickets fallen once the delivery is complete.

commentary.description: English ball-by-ball commentary for the delivery, verbatim from the source — e.g. "FOUR! … driven firmly through the covers". Null if the source has none (lower-tier matches, or deliveries stored before 2026-11-04). Available since 2026-11-04.

shot.description: Direction the ball travelled off the bat, as plotted on a wagon wheel. Null if the source records no direction (an unhit dot ball, a leave, a bye; lower-tier matches). Available since 2026-11-04.

pitchedAt.description: Landing spot of the ball for a pitch map, in the source’s units: y increases with distance from the batter’s stumps (yorker ≈ 25, good length ≈ 41, short ball ≈ 54) and x spans the width of the pitch (values of ≈ 6–26 observed); z is always null. Null if the source has no data. Available since 2026-11-04.

CricketShot.description: Direction and distance of a cricket shot, forming one line on the wagon wheel.

zone.description: Field sector of the shot; null if the source provides only an angle.

angle.description: Shot direction in degrees in the source’s reference frame, seen from a right-handed batter: 0 ≈ square leg, 90 ≈ right behind the keeper, 180 ≈ point, 270 ≈ straight back down the pitch. Unit: degrees.

distance.description: How far the ball went, on a 1–5 scale set by the source: 1–2 near the bat (say, back to the bowler or edged to the keeper), 3 the ring, 4 the deep, 5 the boundary — every four and six. We inferred these bands from the data on 2026-11-04; the source does not document them.

AtBat.description: A single baseball plate appearance. The at-bat list has no outcome field; the result is that of the final pitch (`/at-bats/{atBatId}/pitches`).

id.description: DataSportsAPI id of the at-bat, for use with /v2/fixtures/{id}/at-bats/{atBatId}/pitches. Present since 2026-11-04; lists saved before then show null.

half.description: top: the away team is batting; bottom: the home team is batting.

battingSide.description: Side at bat, derived from the half.

homeWinProbabilityBefore.description: Home win probability before the at-bat on a 0–100 scale, as calculated by the SOURCE (these are not bookmaker odds). Unit: percent.

homeWinProbabilityAfter.description: Home win probability after the at-bat according to the source, 0–100; the away probability is 100 − home. Unit: percent.

DartsSet.description: A single set in darts; a match played in legs consists of one set.

number.description: Set number, always 1 in a legs match.

winner.description: Winner of the set; null in a match played in legs and while the set is still going.

homeSets.description: Sets won by the home side once this set is over; null in a legs match.

awaySets.description: Sets won by the away side once this set is over; null in a legs match.

DartsLeg.description: A single darts leg broken down visit by visit.

number.description: Leg number inside the set (in a legs match, the whole match is one set).

startScore.description: Starting score for each player in the leg (501), as listed by the source.

throwingFirst.description: Side that threw first in the leg according to the source (the throw alternates between legs). The visit list may still open with the other player; this has been seen once on a first leg.

winner.description: Side that won the leg; null while it is still being played.

homeLegs.description: Legs won by the home side in the set once this leg is over.

awayLegs.description: Legs won by the away side in the set once this leg is over.

checkout.description: Score of the visit that won the leg (the checkout); null while the leg is in progress or if the final visit is missing.

DartsVisit.description: One player’s turn at the board: a visit of up to three darts. The source does not report how many darts were thrown.

scored.description: Points scored in the visit, computed as the thrower’s remaining score before minus after. 0 covers both a scoreless visit and a bust, which the source does not distinguish. Null if the drop is impossible for one visit (over 180, meaning the source skipped a visit).

homeRemaining.description: Home side’s remaining score once the visit is done.

awayRemaining.description: Away side’s remaining score once the visit is done.

checkout.description: True if this visit won the leg by bringing the thrower to 0; `scored` then holds the checkout.

first.description: True when first base is occupied.

second.description: True when second base is occupied.

third.description: True when third base is occupied.

InningState.description: Baseball: the current game situation — inning, half, count, outs and runners. It contains no batter or pitcher because the source does not provide them here; find the current at-bat’s in /points `atBats`. The source’s live feed refreshes this state roughly once a minute rather than after each pitch, so the count may trail the game by up to a minute.

half.description: top: the away team is batting; bottom: the home team is batting.

battingSide.description: Side at bat, derived from the half.

balls.description: Number of balls in the current count.

strikes.description: Number of strikes in the current count.

outs.description: Outs recorded in the half-inning; 3 means the half has just finished.

Timeouts.description: Basketball and, since 2026-11-23, American football: the timeouts each side has left and the one being taken right now, as tracked by the source.

homeRemaining.description: Timeouts still available to the home side.

awayRemaining.description: Timeouts still available to the away side.

perTeam.description: Timeouts each side is allotted: for the game in basketball (7 in the NBA), per half in American football (3 in the NFL).

active.description: The timeout in progress; null while none is running. Available since 2026-11-21.

ActiveTimeout.description: Basketball and American football: a timeout in progress. It stays filled for the whole break (in the NBA that is often 2–4 minutes once the TV break is added) and turns null when play restarts. Available since 2026-11-21.

type.description: What kind of timeout it is.

side.description: The side that asked for it; null when the source does not tie it to either team of the fixture.

durationSeconds.description: Length of the timeout (60 in the NBA). Unit: seconds.

clock.description: Game clock at the moment it was called, written as the source writes it: "1:06" means 1:06 to play in the period.

description.description: The source's own line for it, for example "Nets 60 second timeout".

CurrentTyre.description: Tyres currently fitted to a car (available since 2026-11-09).

isNew.description: True for a fresh set, false for a used one; null if the source does not specify.

DragonsByType.description: League of Legends: count of elemental dragons killed, split by element (available since 2026-11-09).

DownAndDistance.description: American football: current down, distance and field position as tracked by the source (available since 2026-11-09). The live feed pushes an update after every play; fields not included in an update keep their previous value.

down.description: The down in play (1–4); null on a kickoff and on the try that follows a touchdown.

yardsToGo.description: Yards needed for a first down (or to the goal line when goalToGo); null when there is no down.

possession.description: Side in possession of the ball.

ballOn.description: Half of the field the ball is in; combined with yardLine, "home 35" means the home side’s 35-yard line.

yardLine.description: Yard line within that half (50 is midfield).

goalToGo.description: True if the goal line is the line to gain (the source calls it isGoalPossession).

playType.description: Kind of play the ball is set up for: scrimmage play, kickoff, try or a free kick after a safety.

VarCheck.description: Football: an ongoing video (VAR) review (available since 2026-11-09).

side.description: Side whose incident (a goal, a penalty, a card) is being reviewed, if the source specifies it; null when it does not name one.

BasketballBonus.description: Basketball: bonus (penalty situation) status for each side, as reported by the source (available since 2026-11-09).

home.description: True when the home side is in the bonus, so the away side’s next team foul awards it free throws.

away.description: True when the away side is in the bonus.

MatchFormat.description: Length of the match in sets / legs / games, if the source states it.

bestOfSets.description: Darts: number of sets in the format ("best of 5 sets"); 1 indicates a legs match without sets.

bestOfLegs.description: Darts: legs per set if `bestOfSets` > 1, otherwise legs in the whole match ("best of 7 legs").

bestOfGames.description: Esports: how many games (maps) the series is played over ("best of 3").

Umpires.description: Baseball only: the umpires working a game.

umpires.description: Crew members in the source’s order, starting with home plate; empty if the source lists none and in other sports. Cricket keeps its officials on the fixture instead: Fixture.umpires and Fixture.tvUmpire, as plain names without position or experience.

Umpire.description: A single umpire working a baseball game.

name.description: Umpire’s full name in the source’s spelling.

position.description: Umpire’s station for this game.

experienceYears.description: Experience in years, according to the source.

Weather.description: Baseball and football: conditions at the venue. The source has weather for these two sports alone (football from 2026-11-23, and only for some matches), so other sports return an empty list. The source reports in °F and mph; we convert to metric (58 °F → 14.44 °C, 5 mph → 8.05 km/h). For a stadium with a roof, the reported weather is still the outdoor one.

observations.description: Measured and forecast conditions in the source’s order, with the observation first; empty if the source has none and in other sports.

WeatherObservation.description: Weather conditions at a venue at a given moment.

at.description: When the observation was made — or, for a forecast, when it was issued.

forecast.description: True if this is a forecast, false if it is a measured observation.

description.description: Conditions as worded by the source ("Overcast"). For display only.

temperatureC.description: Temperature of the air in °C. Unit: celsius.

humidityPercent.description: Relative humidity on a 0–100 scale. Unit: percent.

cloudCoverPercent.description: Share of the sky covered by cloud, 0–100. Unit: percent.

windSpeedKmh.description: Speed of the wind in km/h. Unit: kilometersPerHour.

windDirection.description: Compass point the wind blows from ("SE", "SSE").

EsportsGames.description: Esports: a game-by-game breakdown of a fixture, with map, winner and score, lineups including K/D/A, bans and objectives.

games.description: Each game in sequence; empty before the first game starts and in other sports.

EsportsGame.description: A single game (map) within an esports series.

id.description: The game’s id, which /v2/fixtures/{id}/games/{gameId}/lineups, /bans, /statistics and /rounds expect. A copy stored before 2026-11-19 holds null here until it is refreshed. Available since 2026-11-19.

number.description: Position of the game in the series (1, 2, …).

status.description: Status type of this game (finished, inprogress, notstarted, …).

map.description: Map played ("Dust2"); null for single-map titles (League of Legends), and for an unfinished Counter-Strike game while the source still shows a previous game’s map for it as a placeholder (no map is played twice in a series).

mapId.description: Our identifier for the map, the same in every series it turns up in; null whenever `map` is null. Available since 2026-11-25.

durationSeconds.description: How long the game lasted. Unit: seconds.

winner.description: Side that won the game; null until it ends.

home.description: Home side’s score in this game. The game’s players, bans and objectives have endpoints of their own: /v2/fixtures/{id}/games/{gameId}/lineups, /bans and /statistics.

away.description: Away side’s score in this game. The game’s players, bans and objectives have endpoints of their own: /v2/fixtures/{id}/games/{gameId}/lineups, /bans and /statistics.

homeStartingSide.description: Counter-Strike: which side the home team opened the map on. Every other title reads null, Dota 2 included: its side code at the source is never tied to Radiant or Dire, so we cannot map it. Available since 2026-11-04.

EsportsGameLineups.description: Esports: the player lines of both sides in a single game — K / D / A plus the figures specific to the title. Both lists stay empty until the source publishes them, which happens during the game or up to roughly 40 minutes after it.

home.description: Players of the home side; empty if the source has no lineup.

away.description: Players of the away side; works like home.

EsportsGameBans.description: Esports: the characters banned in a single game of League of Legends or Dota 2. There are no bans in Counter-Strike, where both lists stay empty.

home.description: Characters banned by the home side, in ban order; empty if none are listed.

away.description: Characters banned by the away side; works like home.

EsportsGameStatistics.description: Esports: the objective statistics of both sides in a single game of League of Legends or Dota 2. For Counter-Strike both are null.

home.description: Objectives of the home side; null if the source has none.

away.description: Objectives of the away side; works like home.

EsportsGameRounds.description: Counter-Strike: one map broken down round by round. For any other title the round list is empty.

rounds.description: All rounds played so far, in order, each with its winner, how it ended and the side the home team was on. Empty for other titles, and until the source lists them (it adds a map’s rounds while they are being played).

roundsPerHalf.description: How many rounds a regulation half has (12 under MR12); null if unspecified.

overtimeRoundsPerHalf.description: How many rounds an overtime half has (3 under MR3); null without overtime.

EsportsRound.description: Counter-Strike: a single round on a map.

number.description: Round number within the game, starting at 1; overtime rounds carry on the same count.

outcome.description: The way the Counter-Strike round was decided.

homeSide.description: Side the home team played on in this round (the away team had the opposite one); null if the source does not specify.

RaceCareer.description: Racing: the career history of a driver or constructor (GET /v2/teams/{id}/race-career).

totals.description: Aggregated career figures; null if the source has none.

seasons.description: One entry per season, most recent first.

PenaltyHistory.description: Penalty record of a player for a single league season (GET /v2/players/{id}/penalties).

scored.description: Penalties converted during the league season.

penalties.description: Every penalty taken, in chronological order (oldest first).

PenaltyKick.description: A single penalty taken by a player (football).

fixtureId.description: Fixture in which the penalty was taken.

outcome.description: Result of the kick: goal, save, miss or post.

goalMouthLocation.description: Where the ball finished relative to the goal, from the taker’s perspective.

goalMouth.description: Point at which the ball crossed the goal line, on 0–100 axes following the source’s drawing of the goal; null if not provided.

SeasonDay.description: A date in a league season that has fixtures (GET /v2/leagues/{id}/calendar).

date.description: Calendar day of the season, in UTC.

fixtureCount.description: Number of the league season’s fixtures on that day.

PlayerOfTheSeasonWinner.description: The player of the season named for a league in a past season.

team.description: Team the player represented that season.

rating.description: The player’s mean match rating for the season according to the source, rounded to 2 decimals.

appearances.description: Number of matches in which the player received a rating.

season.description: Season in which the award was won.

GrandSlamResults.description: Results of a tennis player at a single Grand Slam, as returned by GET /v2/teams/{id}/grand-slams.

league.description: The Grand Slam tournament, represented as a league.

years.description: One entry per year, oldest first, going back as far as the source’s records.

GrandSlamYear.description: A tennis player’s furthest progress at a given Grand Slam in a particular year.

season.description: The league season for that year’s edition, if we have its id.

round.description: Deepest round reached, in the source’s wording ("Final", "Semifinals", "Round of 16").

won.description: True if the player took the title.

inProgress.description: True while the edition is still running, meaning the round may still change.

RaceCareerTotals.description: Career totals for a driver or constructor as counted by the source, combining all its series.

racesStarted.description: Number of race starts across the career.

polePositions.description: Number of times starting from pole.

RaceCareerSeason.description: A single season in a driver’s or constructor’s career within one series.

series.description: Racing series the season belongs to.

season.description: The series season; its id is what the `season` parameter expects on the /v2/series/{id}/… endpoints and on /v2/teams/{id}/races.

team.description: For a driver, the team (constructor) driven for that season; null on a constructor’s own row.

position.description: Position in the championship standings; null if unranked (or not yet ranked).

polePositions.description: Number of times starting from pole.

TeamRaceResult.description: One race result in a season for a driver or constructor (from GET /v2/teams/{id}/races).

race.description: The race weekend in question; the result refers to its main race.

position.description: Finishing position of a driver, or a constructor’s ranking among constructors; null if unclassified (see `state`).

points.description: Championship points earned in this race.

state.description: Whether a driver was classified and, if not, why; constructors are always classified.

outReason.description: Reason a driver did not finish, in the source’s words ("Retired"); null when classified.

gridPosition.description: Grid slot the driver started from.

timeMs.description: Driver’s total race time in ms; null if the driver is out, and for constructors. Unit: milliseconds.

gapMs.description: Driver’s gap to the winner; for the winner, and for drivers who are out or lapped, it is null. Unit: milliseconds.

drivers.description: Drivers who raced for the constructor in that event; empty on a driver’s row.

TeamRaceDriver.description: A constructor’s driver in a particular race.

position.description: Finishing position; null if not classified.

gapMs.description: Gap to the winner; for the winner, and for drivers who are out or lapped, it is null. Unit: milliseconds.

state.description: How the race went for this driver: `classified` (given a place), `didNotFinish` (marked out of the race by the source) or `didNotStart` (listed without any result, as when injured or replaced). Available since 2026-11-25.

EsportsGameSide.description: A single team’s score in one esports game. Its players, bans and objectives come from the game’s own endpoints (/v2/fixtures/{id}/games/{gameId}/lineups, /bans, /statistics).

score.description: Score of the side in this game — rounds won in Counter-Strike, kills in League of Legends and Dota 2.

periods.description: Counter-Strike: rounds won in each half (period1, period2), with all overtime rounds combined under `overtime`, so the values sum to the game score. Empty if the source has no breakdown.

EsportsGamePlayer.description: Stat line for one player in one esports game. Only the fields relevant to the title are filled and the rest stay null: League of Legends uses gold / creepScore / level; Dota 2 uses creepScore (last hits) / level / denies / netWorth / goldPerMinute / experiencePerMinute; Counter-Strike uses averageDamagePerRound / headshotKills / kastPercentage / killDeathDifference / firstKillDifference / flashAssists.

firstName.description: Given name of the player from the source's records; `player` carries the in-game handle. Available since 2026-11-25.

lastName.description: Family name of the player from the source's records. Available since 2026-11-25.

alive.description: Counter-Strike, while a map is under way: true if the player is still standing in the current round, false once killed in it. Null for other titles and whenever the source does not report it. Available since 2026-11-25.

role.description: Role the player filled in this game.

gold.description: League of Legends: total gold earned.

creepScore.description: Creeps killed — minions and monsters in League of Legends, last hits in Dota 2.

level.description: Champion / hero level when the game ended (League of Legends, Dota 2).

denies.description: Dota 2: friendly creeps the player last-hit to deny the opponent their gold.

netWorth.description: Dota 2: final net worth in gold (gold held plus items).

goldPerMinute.description: Dota 2: average gold earned per minute of play.

experiencePerMinute.description: Dota 2: average experience earned per minute of play.

averageDamagePerRound.description: Counter-Strike: ADR — hit points of damage dealt per round, on average.

headshotKills.description: Counter-Strike: number of kills scored with a headshot. This is a count capped by `kills`, not a percentage.

kastPercentage.description: Counter-Strike: KAST, the 0–100 share of rounds in which the player recorded a kill or assist, survived, or was traded. Unit: percent.

killDeathDifference.description: Counter-Strike: kills minus deaths; negative if the player died more often than they killed.

firstKillDifference.description: Counter-Strike: opening kills minus opening deaths — an opening duel being the round’s first kill, whether by or on the player. Summed over every player on a map, the values come to 0.

flashAssists.description: Counter-Strike: kills made by teammates on opponents this player had blinded with a flash.

EsportsCharacter.description: A champion / hero / agent that was picked or banned.

name.description: Character name ("Viktor").

EsportsTeamStats.description: One side’s objectives in one game of League of Legends or Dota 2: kills and towers, plus barracks and first blood in Dota 2. Fields that do not exist in the title are null. Counter-Strike has no objectives, so the whole object is null.

gold.description: Total gold earned by the side.

towers.description: Opposing towers taken down (in Dota 2, the towers the opponent lost).

dragons.description: Dragons (drakes) killed according to the source’s count, excluding `elderDragons`.

heraldTaken.description: True if the side secured the Rift Herald.

barracks.description: Dota 2: opposing barracks taken down (those the opponent lost).

dragonsByType.description: League of Legends: elemental dragon kills by element (they add up to `dragons`). Null in other titles, or if the source does not split them. Available since 2026-11-09.

firstBlood.description: Dota 2: true if the side scored first blood, i.e. the opening kill of the game.

Scorecard.description: Complete scorecard of a cricket fixture: every innings, each with a batting card and a bowling card. The ball-by-ball picture (striker, bowler, the over in progress) comes from /v2/fixtures/{id}/events. For other sports the response is 200 with `{ innings: [] }` rather than 404.

innings.description: All innings, in the order played; empty until the first ball is bowled, and in other sports.

ScorecardInnings.description: One cricket innings: totals, the batting card and the bowling card, falls of wicket and partnerships.

inning.description: Innings key in match order (inning1, inning2, …): the second innings of the match is always inning2, regardless of who bats. Uses the same keys as Points.innings.

battingTeam.description: Team at bat in this innings.

bowlingTeam.description: Team in the field in this innings.

runs.description: Innings total, combining runs off the bat and extras.

wickets.description: Wickets fallen, including a batter retired hurt who is unable to return.

overs.description: Overs received, in cricket notation (19.3 means 19 overs plus 3 balls).

extras.description: Runs conceded other than off the bat.

batting.description: Batting card in order of appearance, including did-not-bat entries.

bowling.description: Bowling card in the order the bowlers were used.

fallOfWickets.description: Each fall of wicket in sequence; retirements are not counted as falls.

currentBatter.description: On the innings now being played, the batter marked as current: whoever is about to face, or whoever faced the latest delivery (the partner at the other end is not given). Null for a finished or future innings and on copies stored before 2026-11-27. Since 2026-11-27.

currentBowler.description: On the innings now being played, the bowler marked as current. Null in the same cases as currentBatter. Since 2026-11-27.

ScorecardBatter.description: A single entry on a batting card, listed in batting order.

state.description: Current status of the batter’s innings.

dismissal.description: Manner of dismissal; only set when `state` is out.

description.description: State as phrased by the source ("Not out", "LBW", "Did not bat", "Caught & Bowled"). For display only.

bowler.description: Bowler involved in the dismissal, who is credited with the wicket unless it was a run out. The source also names a bowler on a retired-hurt line.

fielder.description: Fielder involved in the dismissal: whoever took the catch (the bowler for caught & bowled), the wicket-keeper for a stumping, or the fielder who effected a run out.

strikeRate.description: Runs scored per 100 balls, to 2 decimals; null until the batter has faced a ball.

ScorecardBowler.description: A single bowler’s figures from the bowling card; entries follow the order in which they bowled.

bowler.description: The player who bowled these figures.

overs.description: Overs delivered, written the cricket way: 3.4 means three complete overs plus four balls.

runs.description: Runs charged to the bowler: wides and no-balls count towards it, byes and leg byes do not.

wickets.description: Dismissals credited to the bowler; run outs and retirements are excluded.

economy.description: Runs conceded per six-ball over, to two decimal places; null until the first delivery.

FallOfWicket.description: A single entry in the fall-of-wickets list.

wicket.description: Wicket number, counting from 1 for the first dismissal.

runs.description: Team score at the moment the wicket went down.

overs.description: Point in the innings at which it went down, in cricket notation: 4.2 is the second ball of the fifth over, while the sixth ball of that over is written 5 (never 4.6).

Partnership.description: A stand between two batters. Our data source provides these for limited-overs games; multi-day matches frequently come without any.

batter1.description: The first batter in the stand.

batter2.description: The second batter in the stand.

runs.description: Runs the pair put on together.

balls.description: Number of balls the stand lasted.

Extras.description: Runs credited to the batting side that did not come off the bat.

total.description: Combined extras, computed as wides + noBalls + byes + legByes + penalties.

StandingsGroup.description: A single standings table within a season — the overall table, or a conference, division or group.

name.description: The table’s label, such as "Eastern Conference", "Group A" or "NHL".

primary.description: Marks the table that /standings returns when none is requested. Each season has exactly one: the overall table if it exists, otherwise the largest one (for a group stage, the first group).

overall.description: `true` when the table includes all of the season’s teams (a league table); `false` for conference and division tables and for the individual groups of a group stage.

tieBreakRule.description: How ties are broken, as described by our data source.

notes.description: Remarks our data source attaches to the table, in its own words (a team withdrawing from the tournament, for example); an empty list when there are none. Available since 2026-11-20.

scoreUnit.description: Unit behind this table’s scoresFor / scoresAgainst columns. Tables without score columns (cricket) return null.

StandingsRow.description: A team’s line in a standings table. Any column that is irrelevant to the sport is null.

position.description: Position in this table, from 1 to n. When our data source’s positions do not run 1..n, we number the rows ourselves: tables ranked by win share (NBA early in a season) are sorted by win share, then wins, then fewer losses; points tables whose positions skip or repeat a number keep the source’s row order, because its ties are settled by head-to-head results the rows do not show (since 2026-11-23).

team.description: The team this row describes.

wins.description: Total wins, including those in overtime.

draws.description: Drawn games — filled in American football, cricket, football, futsal, handball and rugby, and since 2026-11-23 in darts and snooker. Where a table has no draw column (baseball, basketball, esports, ice hockey, volleyball, water polo, …) the value is null, meaning the column does not exist — not that no draws have happened yet. Water polo leagues that award draws (Serie A1) fill it since 2026-11-25.

losses.description: Total losses, overtime and shoot-out defeats included, so wins + draws + losses = played. In tables where the source counts regulation losses only and keeps the overtime ones apart (the NHL seasons 2013/14 to 2020/21), we add the two together (fixed on 2026-11-23).

overtimeWins.description: Ice hockey only: overtime wins as tallied by our data source. Where shoot-outs are counted separately (the KHL, the NHL’s league table) this covers overtime alone; elsewhere it combines overtime and shoot-out wins. Null where no figure is listed.

overtimeLosses.description: Ice hockey only. Across all NHL tables — league, conference, division, and the home / away tables we compute — it counts losses in overtime and in shoot-outs together, i.e. the NHL’s OTL column, each worth a point. Elsewhere it is the overtime-loss figure our data source reports (for the KHL, overtime losses only).

regulationWins.description: Ice hockey only: wins decided in regulation time, without overtime or a shoot-out, where the source’s table carries the figure (the NHL’s league table, though not its conference or division tables, as well as the KHL, SHL, AHL and the Champions Hockey League, …; also our computed home / away tables when the matches reproduce the source’s figures). Null elsewhere. Available since 2026-11-18.

regulationLosses.description: Ice hockey only: defeats within regulation time, for tables in which the source gives the figure (the NHL’s L column; its OTL column is `overtimeLosses`), or gives them as its losses (the NHL seasons 2013/14 to 2020/21, since 2026-11-23). Null elsewhere. Available since 2026-11-18.

shootoutWins.description: Ice hockey only: shoot-out wins, where the source’s table counts them separately (the KHL; `overtimeWins` then covers overtime alone). Null elsewhere. Available since 2026-11-18.

shootoutLosses.description: Ice hockey only: shoot-out losses, where the source’s table counts them separately (the KHL). Because `overtimeLosses` includes shoot-out defeats, subtract shootoutLosses from overtimeLosses to get the defeats in overtime proper. Null elsewhere. Available since 2026-11-18.

scoresFor.description: How much the team has scored — goals, points, runs, sets, … depending on the table’s `scoreUnit`.

scoresAgainst.description: How much the team has conceded, expressed in the table’s `scoreUnit`.

scoreDifference.description: Difference between the two: scoresFor − scoresAgainst.

points.description: Points in the table; null for tables ordered by win percentage (NBA). Cricket points are exact, fractional bonus points included (a first-class table can read 19.95; since 2026-11-23).

winPercentage.description: Basketball, baseball and American football: proportion of games won, from 0 to 1, calculated the league’s way (in the NFL a tie is worth half a win). Unit: ratio.

secondaryScoresFor.description: Volleyball: rally points the team has won over its matches, next to `scoresFor`, which counts sets. Null outside volleyball, or when the source omits it. Available since 2026-11-25.

secondaryScoresAgainst.description: Volleyball: rally points the team has given away; null in the same cases as secondaryScoresFor. Available since 2026-11-25.

scoringRatio.description: Aussie rules: points scored divided by points conceded, to four decimals. It is the ladder's percentage column over 100 (1.2345 stands for 123.45 %), which separates teams level on points. Null in other sports and until the team has conceded. Unit: ratio. Available since 2026-11-25.

gamesBehind.description: Basketball and baseball: how many games the team trails the leader (the side with the best wins − losses), calculated as ((leader wins − wins) + (losses − leader losses)) / 2. Our data source shows 0 for every row of its EuroLeague tables; the computed NBA home / away tables work it out separately for each table.

streak.description: The team’s ongoing streak in this competition: +3 means three wins in a row, −2 two defeats in a row. Present when our data source’s table includes it (NBA, EuroLeague, Liga ACB, …); null for other tables and for home / away tables.

zone.description: Name of the zone (qualification or relegation) this row sits in — for example "Champions League", "Playoffs" or "Relegation".

notes.description: Remarks our data source attaches to this row, in its own words, such as a points deduction ordered by the federation; an empty list when there are none. Available since 2026-11-20.

averageRating.description: Football only: the mean rating of the team’s players across the season, on the 0–10 scale; null in other sports. Available since 2026-11-20.

noResults.description: Cricket only: matches that ended without a result (abandoned games, which most leagues score as a point each). In first-class (multi-day) tables the source counts drawn matches here too, not under draws. Null in other sports. Available since 2026-11-20.

netRunRate.description: Cricket only: net run rate, the usual tie-breaker: the runs a side scores per over less the runs it concedes per over. Null in other sports. Available since 2026-11-20.

pointsPerGame.description: Averages tables only, the kind that decides relegation on points per game across several seasons (the source's “Promedios”): the points-per-game figure the table is ranked by, to three decimals. Such a table is never the season's main one; it comes as an extra group, so call GET /v2/leagues/{id}/standings with group=all and pick it out by name. Null in all other tables. Available since 2026-11-27.

pointsThisSeason.description: Averages tables: the current season's points that go into the average. Null in all other tables. Available since 2026-11-27.

pointsPreviousSeason.description: Averages tables: last season's points that go into the average; a club that played elsewhere that season scores 0 here, following the source. Null in all other tables. Available since 2026-11-27.

pointsTwoSeasonsAgo.description: Averages tables: the points from two seasons back that go into the average, with the same 0 and null rules as pointsPreviousSeason. Available since 2026-11-27.

form.description: Up to five of the team’s latest results in the part of the competition this table covers (its group or stage, since 2026-11-23; the whole season where no single part covers the table), ordered oldest first so the newest comes last; a home / away table shows only home / away results. Null when our data source gives no form for this table — computed tables, rows stored earlier, or a read that failed.

CupTree.description: Bracket view of a league season’s knockout phase: cup rounds, playoffs or a tennis draw.

name.description: What the bracket is called — "CONMEBOL Libertadores 2026, Knockout stage" or "NBA 25/26, Playoffs", for instance.

currentRound.description: `order` of the round currently being played, or the next one due. Null if our data source does not supply it, or once the bracket is complete (at that point the source points to a round beyond the final one).

rounds.description: The bracket’s rounds, beginning with the first.

CupRound.description: A single round within a knockout bracket.

order.description: Position of the round in the bracket, starting at 1 for the opening round.

name.description: Label our data source gives the round, such as "1/8", "Quarterfinals", "Round of 32" or "Conference finals".

blocks.description: Ties in this round, listed from the top of the bracket down.

CupBlock.description: A single tie in a knockout round — one match, a two-legged tie or a series.

order.description: Where the tie sits in its round, counting from the top as our data source lays out the bracket. Values rise but are not guaranteed to run 1..n: byes or late-entering teams leave gaps (UCL qualifiers 15, 16, 19, …).

home.description: The participant listed first (first-leg home side or higher seed); null if the slot is unfilled.

away.description: The participant listed second; null if the slot is unfilled (a bye).

finished.description: `true` once the tie is settled — a participant has been marked as winner, or our data source reports it finished.

inProgress.description: `true` while any of the tie’s fixtures is live.

startTime.description: Start time of the tie’s opening fixture, in UTC; null if it has not been scheduled.

matchCount.description: Number of fixtures that make up the tie (2 for two legs, 7 for a best-of-7, or 1); 0 for a bye.

fixtureIds.description: Fixture ids for the tie (usable with /v2/fixtures/{id}), in the order our data source gives them.

automaticProgression.description: Flag from our data source indicating the participant advances without playing a fixture.

venue.description: Venue of the tie when our data source provides one (for a one-off final, or the ground of the first leg).

CupParticipant.description: One of the two sides in a knockout tie.

team.description: The team or individual competitor. Null as long as the slot is only a placeholder (“winner of quarter-final 1”); check `fromBlock` in that case.

seed.description: Seeding or entry label in our data source’s own spelling ("1", "Q" for qualifier, "WC" for wild card); null if there is none.

winner.description: `true` if this side won the tie and advanced.

score.description: This side’s score in the tie as reported by our data source: aggregate goals across the legs in football, series games won in basketball and ice hockey, sets in a single tennis match. Null until the tie has been played.

penalties.description: Football only: goals this side scored in a penalty shoot-out, if the tie needed one; otherwise null.

fromBlock.description: The `order` value of the block, one round back (PREVIOUS round), that this participant advanced from. Null in the opening round, or when our data source provides no link and the team did not appear in the previous round (a new entrant).

SearchResult.description: A single search match, ordered by our data source’s relevance ranking. Competitors in tennis and other individual sports come back as `team` results. Since 2026-10-24 managers, referees, racing series and races can match too; since 2026-11-04, fixtures and venues as well, plus a player’s `team`. Agencies (type agency, since 2026-11-23) come only from a type=agency search.

type.description: The kind of entity matched, which tells you which endpoint its id is for.

id.description: Identifier of the matched entity. Which endpoint it works with depends on `type`: /v2/teams, /v2/players, /v2/leagues, /v2/managers, /v2/referees, /v2/series, /v2/races, /v2/fixtures, /v2/venues or /v2/agencies.

name.description: Name to show; for a fixture it is our data source’s "Home - Away" string.

sport.description: Slug of the sport; null for venues, as a venue does not belong to a single sport.

country.description: Where the hit belongs, for team, player, manager, referee and agency hits: for a national team the nation itself, for a player his nationality (since 2026-11-23). League and series hits whose category is a country carry that country too (since 2026-11-25). Null for the remaining types, for categories that are regions, tours or games, and when nothing is given.

category.description: League and series hits: what the competition is filed under, in LeagueRef.category terms, be it a nation ("Kazakhstan"), a wider area ("International"), a tour or a video game title. Other hit types give null. Available since 2026-11-25.

gender.description: Filled for `team` hits (since 2026-11-04) and `league` hits (since 2026-11-25) with the same male / female / mixed value TeamDetail or LeagueDetail would give. Null for the other hit types and for a single athlete flagged mixed; a team that the source calls mixed by name, as in badminton team events, reads `mixed`.

national.description: Team hits: true for a national team, false for a club. Null for every other type. Available since 2026-11-23.

image.description: Image on our CDN — a logo for teams and leagues, a photo for players, managers and referees. Series, races, fixtures and venues never have one; for other entities it is null when no image exists or it is still to be uploaded.

team.description: For player results, the club our data source currently lists them at (since 2026-11-04), and for manager results the team they manage (since 2026-11-24). Null for other types and for anyone without a team (free agents, retired).

position.description: Player hits: his position, in Player.position's terms; null for hits of another type or where the source has none. Available since 2026-11-23.

positionCode.description: Player hits: the source’s own position code ("F", "G", "SS"); null otherwise. Available since 2026-11-23.

retired.description: Player hits: true if the source has the player down as retired; null for hits of another type or where the source is silent. Available since 2026-11-23.

deceased.description: Player hits: true if the source has the player down as deceased; null for hits of another type or where the source is silent. Available since 2026-11-24.

fixture.description: Populated only for `fixture` results (since 2026-11-04) with the key facts of the match; null otherwise.

venue.description: Populated only for `venue` results (since 2026-11-04) with the venue’s city, country and capacity; null otherwise.

race.description: Present on hits of type `race`: the season’s year, the first day and the country of the race. Null on every other type. Available since 2026-11-20.

SearchFixture.description: The match summary carried by a `fixture` search result (since 2026-11-04). For status, score and everything else, call /v2/fixtures/{id}.

home.description: The home side; null until it has been determined.

away.description: The away side; null until it has been determined.

league.description: Competition the match belongs to; null if our data source does not name one.

startTime.description: Planned start time in UTC; null if our data source does not provide one.

status.description: Broad match state when the search ran (no more detailed state is available here); null if our data source gives none.

category.description: Which leaderboard this is — for example football: goals, averageRating, expectedGoals; basketball: rebounds, points; ice hockey: savePercentage, points. It equals `statistic`, except for football’s `mostConceded` / `leastConceded`, which rank goalkeepers by goals conceded with the most / fewest first.

statistic.description: The `statistics` key this leaderboard is built on; each entry’s `value` holds it as a season total. The ordering is our data source’s: counting statistics are generally ranked PER APPEARANCE (value ÷ appearances, so 104 NBA points in 3 games sits above 115 in 4), while ratings and shares rank by the value itself. Treat list position, not `value`, as the rank.

TopPlayerEntry.description: A single player on a leaderboard.

team.description: The player’s team. Baseball leaderboards fill it from our team record (since 2026-11-23) and leave it null for a player who turned out for several teams that season.

value.description: This player’s figure for the ranked statistic, i.e. `statistics[statistic]`.

playedEnough.description: `true` if the player has played enough minutes or games to qualify for the ranking.

statistics.description: All numeric statistics supplied with the ranked entry, under v2 keys that match the per-match key for the same measure (naming conventions for season figures: `…PerMatch` is the total divided by matches, `…Per90` is per 90 minutes, `average…` is a season mean, `…Percentage` runs 0–100, `<key>Against` holds the opponents’ figure, and units are spelled out in the key (`…Seconds`, `…Kmh`)).

TopPerformancesCategory.description: For one statistic, the highest individual match figures recorded in a league season (since 2026-11-09).

category.description: Which per-match player statistic the list ranks. Keys match those in a lineup player’s `statistics` — for football rating, goals, assists, kilometersCovered, topSpeed, keyPass, …; for basketball points, rebounds, …; for ice hockey points, hits, ….

performances.description: At most 10 entries, top performance first in our data source’s ranking — for turnovers, errors and misses that means the highest count, not the lowest.

TopPerformance.description: A single player’s figure from a single match.

fixture.description: The fixture in which the figure was recorded.

value.description: The figure itself, in whatever unit the category’s per-match statistic uses — e.g. rating 0–10, topSpeed in km/h, kilometersCovered in km.

DraftRound.description: A single round of a league draft, as returned by GET /v2/leagues/{id}/draft. Available since 2026-11-09.

picks.description: Picks in this round, sorted by overall pick number.

teamsWithoutPick.description: Clubs that hold no pick in this round because they traded or forfeited it.

DraftPick.description: A single selection in a draft (since 2026-11-09).

overallPick.description: Pick number counted across the entire draft.

round.description: Round in which the pick falls.

pickInRound.description: Pick number counted within its round.

team.description: Club that makes the selection.

tradedFrom.description: For a traded pick, the club that originally owned it; null if it was not traded.

player.description: The drafted player as a record available from /v2/players/{id}; null if our data source has no player entry for them.

prospect.description: The drafted player as described in the draft listing; null while the pick is still to be made.

DraftProspect.description: How the draft itself describes the selected player.

name.description: Name of the prospect as printed in the draft.

position.description: Listed position, using our data source’s abbreviations: G, F, C, FC, … in basketball; QB, WR, OT, … in American football.

topProspect.description: `true` if they were flagged as a top prospect ahead of the draft.

fromTeam.description: The college or former club they come from, when our data source holds it as a team.

fromTeamName.description: Name of that college or club as given in the draft — filled even when fromTeam is null.

TopTeamsCategory.description: One team leaderboard for a season.

category.description: Leaderboard identifier — in football, for example, averageRating, goalsScored or cleanSheets.

statistic.description: The `statistics` key this leaderboard is built on; each entry’s `value` holds it as a season total. The ordering is our data source’s: counting statistics are generally ranked PER APPEARANCE (value ÷ appearances, so 104 NBA points in 3 games sits above 115 in 4), while ratings and shares rank by the value itself. Treat list position, not `value`, as the rank.

teams.description: Teams on the leaderboard, top-ranked first.

TopTeamEntry.description: A single team on a leaderboard.

value.description: This team’s figure for the ranked statistic, i.e. `statistics[statistic]`.

statistics.description: All numeric statistics supplied with the ranked entry, under v2 keys that match the per-match key for the same measure (naming conventions for season figures: `…PerMatch` is the total divided by matches, `…Per90` is per 90 minutes, `average…` is a season mean, `…Percentage` runs 0–100, `<key>Against` holds the opponents’ figure, and units are spelled out in the key (`…Seconds`, `…Kmh`)).

TeamSeasonStatistics.description: Statistics for one team in a given league, season and type.

statistics.description: Totals and averages for the season under v2 keys, which match the per-match key for the same measure (naming conventions for season figures: `…PerMatch` is the total divided by matches, `…Per90` is per 90 minutes, `average…` is a season mean, `…Percentage` runs 0–100, `<key>Against` holds the opponents’ figure, and units are spelled out in the key (`…Seconds`, `…Kmh`)). Football examples: goalsScored, goalsConceded, matches, averageRating, totalShots, averageBallPossession, cleanSheets, …. Ratings are rounded to two decimal places.

SeasonInfo.description: Key facts about a season: running totals and the teams new to it.

statistics.description: Totals for the season under our data source’s own names (football: goals, yellowCards, redCards, homeTeamWins, awayTeamWins, draws, numberOfCompetitors; in other sports numberOfCompetitors may be the only one).

newcomersUpperDivision.description: Newcomers this season that came down from the division above.

newcomersLowerDivision.description: Newcomers this season that came up from the division below.

newcomersOther.description: Newcomers that arrived by any other route.

hostCountries.description: Host nations of a tournament held in particular countries, listed in our data source’s order — Canada, Mexico and USA for the 2026 World Cup, eleven of them for EURO 2020. League seasons usually leave it empty, though a few name their country (Germany for the Bundesliga; USA for MLS and the NFL). `code` is null when the name is missing from our data source’s country list.

hostCities.description: The cities hosting the season, named and ordered as the source gives them; mostly tennis tournaments (an ATP Challenger in Playford reads ["Playford"]). [] when none are named, which is the case for most league seasons. Available since 2026-11-24.

prizeMoney.description: Total prize pool of the season together with its currency (esports tournaments, for example 50,000 USD for DreamLeague Division 2); null when the source states none. Available since 2026-11-18; copies stored earlier show null until they are fetched again.

tier.description: Esports only: the grade the source gives the tournament, as a lowercase letter ("s" is the top tier, followed by "a", "b", "c" …); null in other sports and for ungraded tournaments. Available since 2026-11-18.

PlayerLeagueSeasons.description: A league in which the player has recorded statistics, together with the relevant seasons.

league.description: League or competition reference — the same structure /v2/leagues/{id} and all league lists return.

allTimeSeasonId.description: Where the source keeps one, the id of the league's all-time season. Use it as the `season` of /v2/players/{id}/statistics to read the player's career totals in this league; because those totals cover every season, a plan with a history window is refused with 403 history_not_in_plan. This id never appears in the league's own list of seasons. Null when the source has no all-time season. Available since 2026-11-27.

PlayerStatistics.description: Statistics for one player in a given league, season and type.

statistics.description: Totals and averages for the season under v2 keys, which match the per-match key for the same measure (naming conventions for season figures: `…PerMatch` is the total divided by matches, `…Per90` is per 90 minutes, `average…` is a season mean, `…Percentage` runs 0–100, `<key>Against` holds the opponents’ figure, and units are spelled out in the key (`…Seconds`, `…Kmh`)). Football examples: appearances, minutesPlayed, goals, averageRating, expectedGoals, … — the complete football key list, with what each key measures, is under season statistic keys in this reference. Ratings are rounded to two decimal places.

ratingBreakdown.description: Football: how the season rating breaks down across parts of the game; null if the source gives no breakdown (other sports, or seasons that have no ratings). Since 2026-11-11.

RatingBreakdown.description: Football only, since 2026-11-11: how each part of a player’s game pushed their season rating up or down, as the source works it out — expressed as rating points per match, positive when above a neutral contribution and negative when below (e.g. 0.13 for dribbling, −0.02 for passing).

shotValue.description: Contribution of shooting to the season rating; null when the source omits it (as for goalkeepers).

passValue.description: Contribution of passing to the season rating.

dribbleValue.description: Contribution of dribbling to the season rating.

defensiveValue.description: Contribution of defending to the season rating.

goalkeeperValue.description: Contribution of goalkeeping to the season rating; set for goalkeepers only, null for everyone else.

PlayerFixture.description: An entry in a player’s fixture list: a Fixture plus the player’s personal involvement (`playerMatch`).

startTime.description: When the match starts: initially the planned time, swapped for the actual kick-off once our data source logs it (its live feed delivers this a few minutes after the start). Every endpoint and every WebSocket delta carries the same value.

endTime.description: When the match finished, as the source logged it; null until then and when it logged no time. A cricket Test or other multi-day match is in the date lists for every day from startTime to this. Fixtures saved before 2026-11-26 read null until they are fetched again. Available since 2026-11-26.

league.description: Competition the fixture belongs to. Null if our data source places the fixture in a competition without a matching league — seen on 2026-10-23 in minor regional football, e.g. South Africa’s National Second Division; in that case season and round are null as well.

season.description: The season the source places the fixture in. When a league runs a competition of its own within its season, those games sit in that competition's season: NBA Cup group games belong to "NBA Cup 2026" with its group tables, and the conference and division tables stay with the regular season. /v2/leagues/{id}/seasons lists both.

round.description: Round of the fixture, for competitions organised in rounds.

homeRecord.description: In the US leagues (NFL, NBA, NHL), the home team’s season record as it stands for this game: the "9-4" (in the NHL the W-L-OTL "15-5-2") a broadcast prints beside the team’s name. Null in every other competition. Available since 2026-11-20.

awayRecord.description: The away team’s season record, on the same terms. Available since 2026-11-20.

playerOfTheMatch.description: Cricket’s official player of the match once it has been announced; null before that and in other sports (football’s fan vote is served by /best-players). Available since 2026-11-20.

levels.description: Competition levels our data source assigns to the fixture’s competition ("topCompetitions", "pro", "youth", …), so top-level, professional or youth fixtures can be filtered without keeping a list of leagues. An empty list when it assigns none. Available since 2026-11-20.

tier.description: Tennis only: "lower" marks an event of the Challenger or ITF tier and null a tour-level one; always null in other sports. Available since 2026-11-20.

group.description: Name of the group when the match is part of a group stage ("Group A", as in the round robin of the ATP Finals), otherwise null. The group’s matches are listed by /v2/leagues/{id}/groups/{groupId}/fixtures. Available since 2026-11-20.

stage.description: Where inside the season the source places the match, if that is somewhere below the league: a qualifier ("UK Championship Qualifiers 2026"), a stage like the playoffs ("NWSL, Playoffs") or a fight card. For a one-off tournament that has no league (league null) it carries the tournament’s name (since 2026-11-24). Null when the match sits straight under its league. It is text to show, not a key to match on; fixtures stored before it existed read null until they are fetched again. Available since 2026-11-23.

home.description: The home side; null until it is known (our data source shows a placeholder such as "WQF1", the winner of quarter-final 1).

away.description: The away side; null until it is known (our data source shows a placeholder such as "WQF1").

homeMembers.description: Doubles in tennis, padel, badminton and table tennis: the two players who make up the home pair, ordered as the source gives them. Each of them is a competitor in their own right (a TeamRef of kind individual, at /v2/teams/{id}, with the id their singles matches and rankings use). Null for a single competitor or a team, for a side still to be decided, and when the source’s answer leaves the players out (some lists, and fixtures stored before 2026-11-23 that have not been read since). Available since 2026-11-23.

awayMembers.description: The two players of the away pair, on the same terms as homeMembers. Available since 2026-11-23.

winner.description: Remains null until status.type is finished, and stays null for a fight declared a no contest (`fightResult.method` noContest). If a match was settled on penalties, this is always the shoot-out winner, regardless of our data source (which, on a second leg, names whoever won the 90 minutes). When the source omits a winner, or reports a draw in a sport where draws are impossible, we derive it from the score (matches ending in regular time or overtime; cricket excluded).

venue.description: Where the match is played, if known (lower tiers often have none). Populated on /fixtures/{id} and, when our data source provides it, in date lists. Round, team, player and live lists never include a venue, so null there means "not included" rather than "unknown"; fetch /fixtures/{id} to get it.

clock.description: Running match clock; null if our data source has no clock for the fixture, and after the match ends.

firstToServe.description: Deprecated since 2026-10-23 — mirrors `serving`. Because our data source refreshes it every game / leg, it reflects the side serving (throwing) at present, not the one that served first; use `serving` instead.

serving.description: Tennis, darts and other sports with a serve: which side is serving (throwing) at the moment, refreshed by our data source each game / leg. Null if the source does not report it.

servedFirst.description: Darts: which side threw first in the match (`serving` tells you who is throwing at present). Set when play starts and unchanged afterwards; null before the start, when the source is silent, and for every sport other than darts. Since 2026-11-11.

homeSeed.description: In seeded events — tennis draws, or playoff seeding in basketball and other sports — the seed of the home side ("1", "12") or the way it entered ("Q" qualifier, "WC" wild card, "LL" lucky loser, "PR" protected ranking, …) as printed on the draw. Unseeded sides get null.

awaySeed.description: Seed or entry status of the away side, following the same rules as homeSeed.

homeRanking.description: Ranking of the home side as the source attaches it to the fixture. On UFC bouts: the fighter’s position in the division’s rankings when the bout took place, with 0 for the champion. Tennis players (since 2026-11-23): their ATP or WTA singles position, the one shown in the `atp` / `wta` lists of /v2/rankings rather than the live lists, taken from the source’s most recent reply about the match; doubles pairs and unranked players get null. Other sports (since 2026-11-23): the side’s own standing where the source keeps one, such as the world ranking of a rugby team. Since 2026-11-23 lists carry it as well, as the side’s present-day ranking. For a match that is over, /v2/fixtures/{id} gives the rank the side held on match day; since 2026-11-28 lists show that same match-day rank too, as soon as the fixture has been opened once with /v2/fixtures/{id}, and until then they keep today’s rank (MMA lists: null instead, since today’s rank is homeCurrentRanking). Null when no ranking is attached, as for most fixtures. Available since 2026-11-18.

awayRanking.description: Ranking of the away side; see homeRanking. Available since 2026-11-18.

homeCurrentRanking.description: MMA fixture lists only: where the home fighter sits in his division today, as of the list's latest refresh (0 is the champion). After the bout this can drift away from `homeRanking`, the rank he held on fight night. Null on /v2/fixtures/{id} (which keeps the fight-night rank), in other sports and for a fighter with no rank. Available since 2026-11-25.

awayCurrentRanking.description: Today's division rank of the away fighter; see homeCurrentRanking. Available since 2026-11-25.

note.description: Cricket only: our data source’s match note, which becomes the result line after the finish ("Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by 37 runs"). Intended for display only.

battingSide.description: Cricket only: the side currently batting. Null when no innings is under way, and for all other sports.

fightResult.description: MMA and boxing: how, in which round and at what time the fight ended. Null until status.type is finished, or when our data source gives no method.

fightDiscipline.description: Combat sports: the discipline of this bout when our data source tags one (the `mma` sport includes boxing, kickboxing and Muay Thai cards too). Only some cards get a tag — ONE, Queensbury and some OKTAGON fights, but never UFC or PFL — so null tells you nothing about whether the bout is MMA.

referee.description: Named only if our data source has one (football and some other sports; in cricket, the match referee). You get it on /fixtures/{id}; list endpoints return null since it is not included there.

homeManager.description: Manager or head coach of the home side as named in the source’s fixture, which means whoever leads the team NOW. Up to and during the match that coincides with the person in charge of it; once a finished match is read after a change of manager, the successor appears instead. The managers of the match itself are on /v2/fixtures/{id}/managers. Present on /fixtures/{id}; null in lists.

awayManager.description: Current manager or head coach of the away side; behaves like homeManager.

surface.description: Court surface for tennis matches, returned on /fixtures/{id} and in live lists; other sports get null.

discipline.description: Tennis: singles or doubles, or team for a tie between two nations made of several rubbers (since 2026-11-24; a client that only knows singles and doubles should treat an unknown value as neither). Present on every fixture endpoint, in lists and in WebSocket snapshots; null in other sports and when the source specifies neither. Since 2026-11-11.

toss.description: Cricket only: the toss result, once it has taken place. Populated on /fixtures/{id}; null for every other sport.

umpires.description: Cricket only: the on-field umpires in our data source’s wording (frequently with a country code, e.g. "Asif Yaqoob (PAK)"); null if none are listed, and for every other sport.

tvUmpire.description: Cricket only: the TV (third) umpire, handled the same way as umpires.

previousLegFixtureId.description: For two-legged ties and playoff series: the fixture id of the tie’s preceding leg / game, if our data source links it. Look it up via /fixtures/{id} to get the first-leg score.

parentFixtureId.description: Tennis team competitions (Davis Cup, Billie Jean King Cup): on a singles or doubles rubber, the fixture id of the nations’ tie it is part of, and the tie itself has discipline team. The source makes the link late, often just before the rubber starts, so expect null until then. Null on every other match. Available since 2026-11-24.

matchesInTie.description: For knockout ties and playoff series: the number of matches the tie is decided over, if the source states it — 1 for a one-off match, 2 for a two-legged football cup tie, 7 for a best-of-seven basketball series. Null on a league fixture, whenever the source is silent about it, and on any fixture stored before 2026-11-18 until it is fetched again. Related: previousLegFixtureId. Available since 2026-11-18.

aggregateWinner.description: Set only once a two-legged tie’s return leg has finished: the team that progressed. We take our data source’s verdict; failing that, we use `aggregated` (the higher total goes through) or, when the aggregate is level, the shoot-out. Null in all other cases, including a level aggregate the source leaves unresolved (an away-goals rule). Compare `winner`, which is this match’s winner: after a second leg settled on penalties both point to the shoot-out winner, but otherwise they can disagree (a team can win the second leg yet be eliminated). Only /fixtures/{id} fills it; lists and live snapshots leave it out and may show null.

fightCard.description: MMA and boxing: the bout’s card section, position on the card and weight class, if our data source lists them.

attendance.description: Crowd size, if our data source reports one (observed for NBA and MLB games, often appearing only after the game has started). Populated on /fixtures/{id}; lists return null because it is not included.

matchFormat.description: Match format for darts and esports — best of N sets / legs / games — when our data source provides it. Other sports get null.

inningState.description: Baseball only: the game situation right now — inning, half, balls, strikes, outs and runners on base. It is null while the game is not in progress or interrupted, and in every other sport. WebSocket deltas carry it live.

timeouts.description: Basketball and, since 2026-11-23, American football: timeouts left for each side and the one being taken (`active`), filled only during an in-progress or interrupted game and only if our data source tracks them; null otherwise. WebSocket deltas carry live updates.

downAndDistance.description: American football only: down, distance and field position at this moment. It is null while the game is not in progress or interrupted, and in every other sport. Delivered live through WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-09.

varCheck.description: Football only: an ongoing VAR review; null when there is none, outside play, and for every other sport. Delivered live through WebSocket deltas. Available since 2026-11-09.

bonus.description: Basketball only: the side or sides in the bonus. It is null while the game is not in progress or interrupted, and when our data source gives no value; the source’s live feed lacks it, so you only get it over REST and in lists. Available since 2026-11-09.

finalResultOnly.description: `true` if our data source covers only the final result of this fixture, with no live score, clock or events during play (since 2026-11-09).

stale.description: true for a match the source shows as running although it has gone quiet: no change in 45 minutes, and kick-off longer ago than any match in that sport could take. Such a match is already missing from /v2/livescores and the WebSocket; the date, league, team and fixture endpoints still report the source's status, with this flag set, so treat it as finished rather than live. false otherwise. Available since 2026-11-23.

awarded.description: `true` when the result was awarded rather than played — a forfeit, or a ruling by a disciplinary body or federation. The score is then the awarded one (usually 3–0, or whatever the score was when an abandoned match was allowed to stand), and `status` shows finished just as for a played match. `false` for a result decided on the field and for a fixture still to finish. Fixtures stored before 2026-11-18 carry null until they are fetched again (finished fixtures keep their stored copy). Available since 2026-11-18.

durations.description: Sports played in sets or rounds: the length of every finished period (since 2026-11-04). Null for sports our data source does not time by period (football, basketball, …) and until the first period is over. Delivered live through WebSocket deltas.

awayFirst.description: true where the source lists the visitors first ("Away @ Home": NFL, NBA, NCAA, NHL, AHL and some baseball leagues), false where home leads. Null on fixtures saved before 2026-11-26 until they are fetched again. Available since 2026-11-26.

addedTime.description: Running-clock sports such as football: the announced stoppage minutes per period, keyed like ScoreSide.periods (period1, period2, extra1, extra2), kept after each period ends (clock.injuryTimeMinutes covers only the period in play). Null when none was announced, and on fixtures saved before 2026-11-26 until they are fetched again. Unit: minutes. Available since 2026-11-26.

lineupsAvailable.description: `true` once our data source has published lineups for the fixture, whether predicted or official (`confirmed` on /v2/fixtures/{id}/lineups tells you which); `false` if they were withdrawn. We set it the moment the source’s live feed announces lineups, or when a lineup we fetch contains players. Null means we have no information (no announcement observed, nothing fetched). WebSocket deltas carry it live — on fixture:{id} from before kick-off, and on the list channels once play starts. After the final whistle the flag keeps the value it had during play, in REST and in every list (until 2026-11-26 it turned null there). Available since 2026-11-04.
