x-enumDescriptions.tennisCourt: Tennis: millimetres from the middle of the net. x follows the length of the court (around ±11,900 at each baseline), y its width (around ±4,100 at the doubles sidelines), and z gives how high the ball is above the court surface.
x-enumDescriptions.court: Basketball: 0–100 along the court (x) and across it (y). Home shoots at the x = 100 basket and away at the x = 0 one for the whole game; where the source swaps baskets at half-time, timeline positions are converted into this frame. Since 2026-11-27 timeline y is given as 100 minus the source's figure, because the source measures it from the other sideline than its tracked events; tracked events, timeline entries and the ball therefore agree on y.
x-enumDescriptions.rink: Ice hockey: 0–100 along the rink (x) and across it (y). Home attacks the x = 100 goal and away the x = 0 goal in every period. Which end each team really defended changes by period and the source does not report it, so since 2026-11-12 each side’s positions are mirrored per period according to where its shots went.
x-enumDescriptions.field: American football (since 2026-11-24): yards along the field, 0 at the home goal line and 100 at the away one, for the whole game, so 50 is midfield; the end zones run from −10 to 0 and from 100 to 110. Player frames (since 2026-11-26) add y, 0–100 across the field. Timeline positions stay null; a play’s spot is in TimelineEvent.americanFootball.spot.
x-enumDescriptions.none: Darts (since 2026-11-13): there are no positions at all, so every position is null. Each throw tells you which bed it hit instead (TimelineEvent.darts).

DartsRing.description: Which scoring area of the board a dart hit.

x-enumDescriptions.single: A single bed: the segment’s number counts once.
x-enumDescriptions.double: The narrow outer ring: the number counts twice. Every leg has to be finished on a double.
x-enumDescriptions.treble: The narrow inner ring: the number counts three times.
x-enumDescriptions.outerBull: The ring around the bullseye, worth 25.
x-enumDescriptions.bull: The bullseye itself, worth 50; it counts as a double.
x-enumDescriptions.miss: Scores 0: the dart landed outside the scoring area or bounced out.

DartsBed.description: For a dart in a single, which of the two single beds it hit.

x-enumDescriptions.inner: The single bed nearer the centre, from the outer bull out to the treble ring.
x-enumDescriptions.outer: The single bed nearer the edge, from the treble ring out to the double ring.

TableTennisPointFlag.description: What a table tennis point brought about (TimelineTableTennis.flag). Since 2026-11-24.

x-enumDescriptions.gamePoint: After this point one player can win the game with the next.
x-enumDescriptions.matchPoint: After this point one player can win the match with the next.

AmericanFootballOutcome.description: How an American football play ended (TimelineAmericanFootball.outcome). Each value belongs to the play types named before the colon. Since 2026-11-24.

x-enumDescriptions.complete: pass: caught; rush: the runner was stopped in play.
x-enumDescriptions.returned: kickoff / punt: the receiving team ran it back.
x-enumDescriptions.touchback: kickoff / punt (or a run): dead in the end zone, so play restarts at the receiving team’s own 20 or 25.
x-enumDescriptions.fairCatch: punt: caught with no return attempted.
x-enumDescriptions.downed: kickoff / punt: stopped by the kicking team where it came to rest.
x-enumDescriptions.outOfBounds: kickoff / punt: went out of bounds.
x-enumDescriptions.muffed: kickoff / punt: the receiver could not hold on to it.
x-enumDescriptions.recovered: fumble: the team that fumbled got the ball back.
x-enumDescriptions.turnover: fumble: the opponents took the ball.
x-enumDescriptions.declined: penalty: turned down by the team it would have helped.
x-enumDescriptions.offsetting: penalty: fouls by both teams cancel each other out.
x-enumDescriptions.callStands: videoReview / challenge: the call on the field stays.
x-enumDescriptions.callOverturned: videoReview / challenge: the call on the field was changed.
x-enumDescriptions.passing: touchdown: a pass into the end zone.
x-enumDescriptions.interceptionReturn: touchdown: an intercepted pass carried back.
x-enumDescriptions.fumbleReturn: touchdown: a recovered fumble carried back.
x-enumDescriptions.other: An outcome the source names that we have not mapped yet.

AmericanFootballRole.description: The part a player took in an American football play, as AmericanFootballPlayer.role records it. Since 2026-11-24.

x-enumDescriptions.passer: Threw the pass; also the quarterback who was sacked.
x-enumDescriptions.target: The intended receiver of a pass that was not caught.
x-enumDescriptions.kicker: Took the kick: kickoff, punt, field goal or extra point.
x-enumDescriptions.recoverer: Came up with the loose ball.

TimelineOp.description: How a timelineEvent frame changes the timeline you keep.

x-enumDescriptions.upsert: Insert the event, or overwrite the one you already hold under that key, because the source corrected it or because its position was flipped into the home → x = 100 frame after more shots of that period came in.
x-enumDescriptions.remove: Delete the event with this key, because the source took it back (a goal that was chalked off, a shot logged twice).

BaseballHalf.description: Top or bottom of an inning.

x-enumDescriptions.top: The first half of the inning, with the away side at bat.
x-enumDescriptions.bottom: The second half, with the home side at bat.

WsErrorCode.description: Codes that a WebSocket `error` frame can carry.

x-enumDescriptions.bad_frame: The frame is not valid JSON, does not match any known shape, or is missing a required field; `message` names that field (e.g. "channel: required").
x-enumDescriptions.unknown_channel: The channel name is not one we offer, or its sport slug is unknown.
x-enumDescriptions.channel_forbidden: Your plan’s tier does not include this channel.
x-enumDescriptions.unknown_league: league:{id} refers to a league id DataSportsAPI never issued (take ids from /v2/leagues or from a fixture’s league). The REST API returns 404 not_found for the same id.
x-enumDescriptions.unknown_fixture: The id in fixture:{id} — or in odds:{id} (from 2026-11-04) or tracking:{id} (from 2026-11-12) — is not a fixture DataSportsAPI issued; REST answers 404 not_found for that id. It does not count as one of your channels.
x-enumDescriptions.unknown_race: race:{id} does not point to a race: it is a season or session id, or an id DataSportsAPI never issued. /v2/races/{id} returns 404 for the same id. It does not count as one of your channels.
x-enumDescriptions.unknown_team: team:{id} refers to a team id DataSportsAPI never issued (take ids from a fixture’s home / away or from /v2/teams). The REST API returns 404 not_found for the same id. Available since 2026-11-04.
x-enumDescriptions.history_not_in_plan: You subscribed to fixture:{id}, odds:{id}, tracking:{id} or race:{id} for a match that kicked off, or a race that began, before the first day of your plan's history; `message` names that day. A REST call for that id gets 403 history_not_in_plan too. A refused channel is left out of maxChannels. Available since 2026-11-27.
x-enumDescriptions.not_subscribed: A resync / unsubscribe targeted a channel this connection has not joined.
x-enumDescriptions.too_many_channels: This connection has reached its maxChannels limit.
x-enumDescriptions.snapshot_failed: Building the snapshot failed; retry with resync. For league:{id}, this also happens when the league id could not be verified at that moment, in which case subscribe again.
x-enumDescriptions.rate_limited: This connection sent over 60 frames within 10 seconds; further frames are discarded until the window resets.

PeriodKey.description: periodN: Regulation period number N. What a period is depends on the sport: a half in football, rugby, handball, futsal, minifootball and bandy; a quarter in basketball, American football, water polo and aussie rules; a period in ice hockey and floorball; a set in tennis, volleyball, table tennis, badminton and padel; an inning in baseball; a round in combat sports; a map / game in esports; a leg / frame block in darts and snooker. inningN: Cricket only: innings number N. extra1: Football and futsal: the opening half of extra time. extra2: Football and futsal: the closing half of extra time. overtime: Every overtime period summed into one value (American football, basketball, handball, ice hockey, water polo, …), as used by scores, status.period and incidents. In baseball it holds the runs scored in extra innings, and only when the source provides no inning-by-inning split (period10, …). overtimeN: Overtime number N, where the source numbers them separately (since 2026-11-23): in match statistics, in play by play and on ice hockey shots. A single overtime is still overtime1, and a basketball game that needs two has overtime1 and overtime2. Scores, status.period and incidents keep the combined `overtime`. penalties: The penalty shoot-out, which appears only as a `status.period` value; its score is kept in ScoreSide.penalties, not under a `periods` key.

Export.description: A season export (Business and up). Poll it until status is ready or failed.

league.description: Our league id, as you sent it.

season.description: The season id, as you sent it.

error.description: Why a failed export failed or, on a ready one, which parts could not be read (e.g. "not included: topPlayers").

fixtureCount.description: How many fixtures the export holds, once it is ready.

finishedAt.description: When it became ready or failed.

files.description: One entry per file; empty until the export is ready.

linksExpireAt.description: When the url values in files stop working: an hour after you read them.

ExportFile.description: One file of a ready export.

name.description: File name, e.g. fixtures.parquet or season.json.

url.description: Signed download link; no API key needed, valid until linksExpireAt.

Error.description: The body of every failed request. Branch on error.code; the message may be reworded.

code.description: Stable, snake_case code, e.g. not_found. Part of the contract.

message.description: A readable sentence for logs; never parse it.

historyFrom.description: history_not_in_plan only: the first day your plan can read.

upgradeUrl.description: rate_limited and quota_exceeded only: the address of the pricing page.
